  - depends on: F-244
  - acceptance: A spring-mounted piston driving a fluid column at an added-mass to body-mass ratio of at least 1 oscillates at omega = sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) within 2 percent, the amplitude at successive same-side turning points never grows (ratio <= 1 + 1e-3) over at least 10 periods, and the explicit coupling of ADR 0033 D7 grows or diverges on the same case (registered before the run); halving dt changes the frequency by <= 0.5 percent
  - note: Split from F-244 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size L. Needed for light structures; not on the first fan path. DONE (ADR 0250, registered 2026-11-12 before the code, merged 2026-11-12): opt-in library function rcfd_fv::fsi::strong_step (new module, nothing calls it; pimple.rs, pimple/moving.rs, sixdof.rs, ale.rs, rcfd-api and the case schema untouched; the loose coupling of ADR 0033 D7 is unchanged and with max_iterations = 1 the strong step equals it bit for bit). Within a time step it iterates on the fluid force and moment held over the body step, each iterate restarting body and flow from t_n, with a fixed or an Aitken relaxation; the Aitken start and the best fixed factor come from an added-mass estimate, 2M/(2M + m_a) (the added-mass term of the body equation written as a relaxation; the half belongs to RK4 with a constant force and a wall velocity taken from the displacement). Derived and measured: the loose loop as built is unstable above a mass ratio of 2, not 1, with a growth of sqrt(ratio/2) per step whatever the time step (flow: stable at 1.5, diverges at 3 and 4; growth 1.39 per step at ratio 4 for T/100 and T/200); the gain of the sub-iteration is 1 + ratio/2 (measured 2.952 at ratio 4), so a fixed factor converges below 4/(2 + ratio). Acceptance case, the spring-mounted piston of ADR 0211 at ratio 4 (M = 0.01, 11.5 periods): omega_m/omega 1.005081 at T/100 (limit 2 %), dt halving 1.7e-5 (limit 0.5 %), successive same-side turning points fall by 7.5 % a period at T/100 and 3.9 % at T/200 and never grow (lag of dt/2 of the end-of-step force), the loose coupling passes 10 X at step 28 (T/100) and 31 (T/200) and ends with the piston through the outlet; 3.0 flow solves per step at a tolerance of 1e-8, never more than 4 (cap 20). Also met: ratio 20 (1.005968, 3.25 solves per step), agreement with the loose coupling at ratio 0.2 (frequency within 2.0e-4, the trajectory difference halves with dt), the restart of an iterate bit-exact, refusals leave flow and body untouched, the existing sixdof, sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244, ale_flows and ale_gcl suites pass unedited; eight library mutations each failed their tests. Amendment 1 (before any run): the unrelaxed-iteration control was registered with a cap it cannot reach and was replaced by one with cap 10. Not delivered: selecting the coupling from a case file (no key; follow-up item), Newmark with the sub-iteration, a rotating body in a flow. Found, not fixed: the discrete added mass of the column is 1.25 % below rho A L0 at every ratio (the +0.1 % of ADR 0211, +0.5 % here); follow-up item. Open: ADR 0250 Q1 (reword "ratio of at least 1" to 4), Q2 (case key), Q3 (stop or warn at the cap), Q4 (added-mass deficit), Q5, Q6. A cloud of 20 000 tracer parcels (tau = 1e-3 T_L) on the k-epsilon and SST models' homogeneous fields is within 0.04 to 0.79 percent of both forms at 0.25, 1, 4 and 10 T_L (limit 5 percent), an inertial cloud (tau = T_L) within 1.1 percent; the tree equals the library bit for bit on non-uniform fields, and the transient and two-way refreshes give the fields of the right time level bit for bit. Reaction (`rcfd_particles::reaction`, `Tracker::set_reaction`): a first-order kinetic surface reaction with an inert residue (a choice of the ADR, Q7), linear shrinkage to 1.7e-14, the mass of the solid and of each gas species measured on the parcel side and on the carrier side within 2.0e-14 at every step of a run with wall hits (limit 1e-10).   - depends on: F-243
  - acceptance: A plane pulse leaving through a sponge layer at 0, 30, 45 and 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; a case without a sponge is bit-identical.
  - gap: Case-schema wiring is not done (a new key needs an approved edit of a registered hash test); it goes with F-330. Open in ADR 0237 addendum 1: the wiring, max_dt knowing the explicit source, moving meshes.

Built: an opt-in sponge layer of the compressible solver (rcfd-fv sponge.rs, `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge`), in two forms: `Plain` (every conserved variable relaxes to a reference state) and `Matched` (a perfectly matched layer of linear acoustics about a state at rest: mass, energy and normal momentum relax, the tangential momentum is forced through one scalar of memory per cell); polynomial profile, peak rate from the wanted two-way attenuation (`rate_max_for_reflection`). The registration showed beforehand that the plain form cannot reach 1 percent at 45 and 60 degrees in a practical thickness (175 pulse widths at 60 degrees), so the acceptance is met by the matched form. Measured (limit 1 percent, layer of 40 cells, largest difference to a run on an extended grid against the incident peak): normal incidence 9.2e-7 in front of the Thompson boundary and 1.1e-6 in front of a rigid wall; one isolated plane pulse 2.4e-5 at 30 degrees and 1.4e-4 at 45 degrees; pulse trains in a rigid duct 1.2e-4, 2.8e-4, 1.2e-3 at 30, 45, 60 degrees (the Thompson boundary alone 0.081, 0.196, 0.372; the plain form at 45 degrees 0.150). Without a sponge the solver is bit-identical (the F-258 bit records and the ADR 0233 tests pass unedited; a set-and-cleared sponge and a zero-rate sponge give the same bits). Six mutations caught. One amendment: the first oblique set-up (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory) measured 3.8e-2, 6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 and was diagnosed as a defective set-up before the corrected runs; its tests are kept as ignored records. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of a registered hash test; this is why the status is partial). Limits: the matched form is one planar layer with a reference at rest, does not damp waves along the layer (a transient inside the layer leaves transverse standing waves in a rigid duct, the 4 to 9 percent of the first set-up) and has a memory without decay; the plain form is quiet only near normal incidence; 60 degrees is checked with pulse trains, not with an isolated pulse; explicit source (`rate dt` well below 2.5, `max_dt` does not know it); not on moving meshes; Cartesian grids, gas at rest. Open questions in ADR 0237 addendum 1 (wiring, an isolated pulse at 60 degrees, memory decay and damping along the layer, `max_dt`, moving meshes). Follow-ups (recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): the wiring goes with F-330; F-340 (memory decay, damping along the layer, corners); F-341 (moving meshes).

- [~] **F-334** Overset: the first-order error term of the calculated component cells
  - depends on: F-314
  - acceptance: Set-up RL of ADR 0232 (component at rest, fringe phase locked) on levels 1 to 4: the root mean square of the error of the calculated component cells converges at order 1.7 or more between successive levels, or the ADR names the source of the first-order term (coefficient 1.0e-4) with a number.
  - gap: The order check is missed: RL on levels 1 to 4 converges at 1.277, 1.166, 1.626 against 1.7. The source is named (truncation of the linear donor interpolation), but the background-fringe response is still first order (F-349) and RL is to be added to F-336's acceptance.
  - note: From ADR 0232 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0246 (registration of F-334, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change. The order check is missed: RL on levels 1 to 4 gives 1.549e-4, 6.39e-5, 3.98e-5, 2.49e-5 in the root mean square of the calculated component cells, orders 1.277, 1.166, 1.626 (limit 1.7); the fit of ADR 0232 predicted 2.86e-5 at level 4. The source is named: the truncation of the linear donor interpolation. With stencils exact for biquadratic fields on both fringes (nine cells, test code) the error is 3.24e-4, 8.55e-5, 3.90e-5, 2.23e-5, orders 1.922, 1.935, 1.950, and equals the error of the background alone. The error with the library stencils is the sum of that part and of the response to the truncation, which is 1.35 to 1.90 times larger, opposed to it (cosine -0.96 to -0.88) and converges at 1.693, 1.588, 1.800; they cancel to 88 to 96 percent, so the library stencils give the smaller error at levels 1 and 2 and the lower order. The coefficient 1.0e-4 is the increment per level of that response times L^2 (1.04e-4, 0.98e-4, then 0.38e-4). Its part from the background fringe is of first order on levels 1 to 3 (4.9e-5, 2.2e-5, 1.41e-5: 1.153, 1.093) and still growing at t = 0.5; the part from the component fringe converges at 1.782, 1.698. Ruled out with numbers: a time error, the single-mesh solution, the outer boundary of the component, the reference cell, the interpolated pressure and the convection (the error is linear in the amplitude to 0.07 percent), a mass defect, the flux at the fringe faces, the transient Rhie-Chow term; with coincident meshes the coupling gives the background alone to 7e-9. Traced by ADR 0340 (F-349): the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed on the calculated cells through a resistance proportional to nu / h (a flux defect held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D), so the response per unit of truncation grows with the refinement; the truncation of the background fringe of RL also alternates between odd and even levels. Controls held, four mutations caught. Follow-ups (ADR 0246 questions 2 and 4, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-336 with RL added to its acceptance, and F-349 on the response to the background fringe.

- [x] **F-336** Overset: donor interpolation of higher order
  - depends on: F-134, F-334
  - acceptance: An opt-in donor interpolation that reproduces quadratic fields; with it the largest error over the calculated and fringe cells of TG_L converges at order 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 3 with dt proportional to h^2, the root mean square of the error of the calculated component cells of RL of ADR 0232 converges at order 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 4 (ADR 0246 TQ: 1.922, 1.935, 1.950 with test-supplied stencils), the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219 holds, and the default stencils and results are bit-identical.

Built: an opt-in of rcfd_mesh::overset, Overset::set_donor_interpolation(DonorInterpolation::Quadratic): the stencil of a fringe cell is the donor and the calculated cells that share a point with it (9 on quadrilaterals, 27 on hexahedra; a fringe or hole cell is never a donor), with the weights of the weighted least-squares quadratic (the minimum of sum w^2/omega under the reproduction of the 6 monomials in 2-D, 10 in 3-D, by a pivoted Householder QR). The weights sum to one, can be negative (smallest -0.067, sum of absolute values 1.40 on a whole block) and are not clipped; a stencil with fewer cells than monomials, of deficient rank or with a sum of absolute values above 4 keeps the linear stencil and is listed (Connectivity::fallbacks, OversetInfo::n_fallback), and a step whose interpolated rAU is not positive is refused. Met: quadratics are reproduced to 1e-15 on Cartesian, distorted, O-grid and sheared 3-D donor meshes; the truncation converges at 3.00; TG_L with dt proportional to h^2 converges at 1.993 and 2.000 on levels 1 to 3 (largest error 7.68e-4, 1.93e-4, 8.58e-5, now in a background cell at the domain boundary; 1.0785e-3, 3.514e-4, 1.712e-4 with the linear stencils); the calculated component cells of RL converge at 1.916, 1.924, 1.952 on levels 1 to 4 (3.20e-4, 8.48e-5, 3.89e-5, 2.22e-5); the uniform flow holds to 1.1e-14; coincident meshes give the background alone to 6e-12; no fallback and no unconverged solve on the registered set-ups; without the opt-in the stencils are those of ADR 0219 bit for bit, Q0 and the records R2 hold. Said plainly: on the two coarsest levels of RL the calculated component cells have 2.07 and 1.33 times the error of the linear stencils (the cancellation of ADR 0246), 0.98 and 0.89 at levels 3 and 4. Limits: a donor next to a wall or to its own fringe ring falls back to the linear stencil; no flow run of the cylinder case or in 3-D with the opt-in. Six mutations caught. Found on the way: the donor search of F-134 finds no donor in cells with non-planar faces. Open for the maintainer: whether the opt-in should become the default (ADR 0251 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0251 questions 2 and 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-352, F-353. Open: question 1 (the quadratic interpolation as the default changes a default). no flow run in 3-D with the opt-in; the cylinder case TR with it is F-353 (ADR 0259: acceptance met, no fallback, mean drag error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3 of the linear stencils, recommendation against the default)

- [~] **F-340** Matched sponge layer: memory decay, damping along the layer, corners
  - depends on: F-331
  - acceptance: The set-up D record of ADR 0237 (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct) falls below 1 percent within its registered window; a constant pressure offset with a gradient along the layer gives a bounded tangential momentum over 100 transit times of the layer; a pulse leaving through the corner of two layers reflects less than 1 percent; an isolated plane pulse at 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; the checks A0, A30b, A45b, A60b, X1 and X45 of ADR 0237 still meet 1 percent.
  - gap: Clause 1 is missed: set-up D stays at 3.7e-2, 6.1e-2, 8.6e-2 at 30, 45, 60 degrees with the shift (2.2e-2, 3.6e-2, 4.2e-2 with along = 0.05) against 1e-2, and no matched layer damps it. Open: what to do with clause 1, the default shift in the F-330 wiring, whether to keep along, a 3-D corner run.
  - note: From ADR 0237 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0248): four of the five clauses are MET IN THE LIBRARY, clause 1 is MISSED with a diagnosis that the registration gave before the runs. Built (rcfd-fv sponge.rs, opt-in, `Plain` and `Matched` untouched): `SpongeForm::MatchedShifted(MatchedOptions { normal, shift, along, second })`, the matched layer as a complex coordinate stretching with (i) a complex frequency shift `shift` (the memories decay: under a held pressure the memory and the force along the layer saturate at p'/a instead of growing; below omega ~ a the layer does not absorb and it leaves a static offset alone), (ii) a second planar layer with an orthogonal normal for a corner (`Sponge::corner`: the same memory, one product term, the force of each layer on the momentum along the other's normal; a second memory for an edge in three dimensions), (iii) a damping of the momentum along the layer `along` (a mismatch with a measured price); `Sponge::planar_shifted`, `CompressibleSolver::sponge_memories` and `set_sponge_memories`. Measured with shift 0.25/s (0.05 c/L) and along 0 on the 40-cell layer of ADR 0237 (limit 1 percent, largest difference to a run on an extended grid against the incident peak): an isolated plane pulse at 60 degrees 8.1e-4 (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 8.0e-4; 705 000 and 770 000 cells, the set-up of X45 with tails of 3.5 pulse widths and a reference grid shortened by a causality argument that a model confirmed to 12 digits); a quarter of a cylindrical pulse through two layers and their corner 5.3e-5 (no sponge 0.058, one layer 0.029); the checks of ADR 0237 repeated with the shift: A0 9.4e-7 (1.2e-6 in front of a rigid wall), A30b, A45b, A60b 3.1e-4, 3.6e-4, 1.3e-3, X1 2.3e-5, X45 1.4e-4; a closed box with a pressure offset varying along the layer over 100 transit times: momentum along the layer at most 3.0 delta/c and not growing (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 3.2 and not growing either: in a run neither form grows, the difference is under a held pressure, checked by algebra to 4e-6). Without the options the new form produces the bits of `Matched`; the existing compressible, F-258, ADR 0233, ADR 0237 and ADR 0243 tests pass unedited. Eight mutations caught. MISSED, clause 1: the set-up D record (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct) stays at 3.7e-2, 6.1e-2, 8.6e-2 at 30, 45, 60 degrees with the shift (3.8e-2, 6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 without) and at 2.2e-2, 3.6e-2, 4.2e-2 with along = 0.05, against 1e-2; kept as three ignored known_miss records. Diagnosis (ADR 0248 DR12, a scratch model predicted the five numbers within 20 percent before the runs): the ringing sits at the cut-off frequencies of the duct; a field that does not vary across the layer solves the equations of every matched layer, so no matched layer damps it; a damping along the layer is a mismatch that reflects about 1.3 along of a pulse at 60 degrees whatever its frequency (along = 0.05 measured 4.4e-2 of the steady train at 60 degrees), and the strength needed to remove the ringing within the registered window costs far more than 1 percent. Not a parameter that could be tuned at this thickness. Limits: linear acoustics about a state at rest; one layer or two orthogonal ones (no corner of three layers; the three-dimensional edge is checked by algebra only); explicit source; not on moving meshes; not with a mass-spring-damper wall; library only (the wiring goes with F-330); Cartesian grids. Open questions in ADR 0248 addendum 1 (what to do with clause 1; a default for the shift in the wiring; whether to keep `along`; a corner run in three dimensions). Open: the default shift in the F-330 wiring (a default; ADR 0248 question 2). The clause-1 follow-up (a plain damping zone behind a thicker layer) is proposed in ADR 0248 only for when a ducted case shows the ringing; no item added. Maintainer (2026-11-18): held. The default change named above is not approved now; it would move existing flow results and waits until the fan path needs it. The other questions listed above are closed by the lead on their written recommendations.

Built (rcfd-fv, opt-in): `sponge::SpongeFrame { StaticMesh (default: step_ale refuses a sponge, as before), AttachedToMesh }` and `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge_frame`. When attached, the rates (of both layers of a corner) and the memories belong to the cells and move with them; the reference stays a lab-frame state; the memory of a cell is the time integral of p - p_ref along its path; and `step_ale` adds the source at the volume of each Runge-Kutta stage, which keeps the damping consistent with the geometric conservation law (a uniform offset decays as exp(-rate t) for any deformation). `replace_mesh` still refuses a sponge, because the solver has no map from old to new cells and a matched layer reset under a wave rings: clear it, replace the mesh, then set a new sponge and the caller's mapped memories. Measured: a uniform reference state on the deforming set-up U of ADR 0207 stays within 3.3e-15 over 121 to 136 steps in the plain, matched and shifted-corner forms (limit 1e-12); the ADR 0237 tube with both grids translating at Mach 0.2 reflects 9.6e-7 (plain and matched, Thompson end and pressure-release end) and 9.8e-7 (shifted) against 1e-2; on a mesh whose cells change volume by 16 percent a uniform offset decays within 3.1e-7 of exp(-2 t), the memory is within 8.3e-6 of its integral, and the shifted form is within 1.2e-7 of the static step. `step_ale` is bit-identical without a sponge, with a sponge set and cleared, with the frame setting alone and with zero-rate sponges; the F-258 bit records, the ADR 0233, 0237, 0243 and 0248 tests and baseline_hashes pass unedited. Seven mutations caught. One amendment: the control without sponge (pressure release, peak measure) gave 0.864 against 0.9. It was diagnosed as the peak loss of a pulse that the reflection on the moving mesh narrows to 2/3, and replaced by the time-integral ratio, 0.9995 (that value was seen in the diagnostic before the amendment; disclosed). Limits: attached frame only (no layer fixed in space); on a moving mesh the matched forms are matched at normal incidence only, because the medium moves relative to the layer (oblique incidence, motion along the layer and rotation not checked); library only, like the sponge itself; two-dimensional checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the no-sponge control NCr missed its registered limit (0.864 against 0.9) and its replacement NCr2 was registered after a diagnostic had shown its value, so it is not blind; done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0265 Q1). ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).

  - acceptance: A specification of the card (fields, sign, required surface elements) from an open source is placed in the repository; the deck writes it beside RCFDQ; the tube heat rate after a round trip through the repository reader matches the fluid heat rate to 0.1 percent
  - note: Priority P3. Size S. Area: io. Opened by ADR 0244: RCFDQ is the repository's own card; no vendor heat-flux card layout is specified in the repository, so none was written. NEEDS THE USER: an open specification of the card has to be placed in the repository first (clean-room rule). Maintainer (2026-11-18): parked until an open specification of the card is in the repository. Not on the fan path.
- [~] **F-348** Anisotropic (directional) refinement: a lattice with per-axis levels
  - depends on: F-343
  - acceptance: A lattice with per-axis refinement levels gives valid closed meshes for random directional marks (validate, closure, volume) and transfers linear fields exactly; on the ADR 0247 suction layer a directional run reaches the isotropic adapted error E(A) with at most half of its 3841 cells; the isotropic AmrMesh paths stay bit for bit.
  - gap: The acceptance numbers are met (1547 cells against the limit 1920). Open: the case key (F-438) and cells spent along x in early cycles (R4); the item stays partial because two registered supporting checks missed and were corrected by amendment.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0267, 2026-11-12): rcfd_mesh::adapt::aniso::AnisoMesh, a second lattice with one refinement level per axis (AxisLeaf, AxisMark; AmrMesh untouched): faces are the intersections of the sides of two leaves, with the corners of all face rectangles in the vertex set, so cells are closed for any tiling by dyadic boxes; optional balance of one level per refined axis across every face (at most 2 faces per side in a slab, 4 in 3-D); the existing Transfer and transfer_field. Random directional marks on a graded 3-D box, a slab and a box refined along two of three axes give valid closed meshes (validate, closure and volume to 1e-13) and linear fields transfer to 4.4e-16; on isotropic marks the mesh, the transfer and the adaptive loop equal AmrMesh's bit for bit. Directional criterion in rcfd_fv::adaptive (axis_variations, directional_axes with theta = 1/2, directional_target_marks, run_adaptive_simple_directional and _target). On the ADR 0247 suction layer the directional run has error 0.00298 with 1547 cells against the isotropic 0.01159 with 3841 (limit: at most 1920 cells); held at the isotropic finest size it reaches 0.01158 with 960 cells; with the axis choice inverted 1.18. ADR 0054, 0242 and 0247 tests pass unedited (the heavy ones included); ten mutations each failed their tests. Partial by the rule because two registered supporting checks missed and were corrected under amendments: pair coarsening in 3-D can leave a five-box tiling of a cell that it cannot merge further (valid mesh; slabs return to the base), and the fast layer test on an 8 x 8 base (cell Peclet 10) had no converged solution on its first directional mesh (replaced by a 16 x 16 base). Open: a box merge for 3-D coarsening (R2), the case key (R5), cells spent along x in early cycles (R4). Follow-ups: F-438 (case key), F-439 (three-dimensional box merge). The box merge is delivered by F-439 (ADR 0341, 2026-11-12): repeated all-axes box coarsening returns any state, the five-box tiling included, to the base. Maintainer (2026-11-18): the open questions above that were listed before the standing instruction of 2026-11-11 are closed by the lead on their written recommendations, except any that would change a default result, a golden or a hash table or that needs a source; those stay as they are.
- [~] **F-349** Overset: the response to the truncation of the background-fringe interpolation
  - depends on: F-334
  - acceptance: The response R_b of ADR 0246 (the difference of the RL runs with the library stencils and with a third-order interpolation on the background fringe: 4.87e-5, 2.19e-5, 1.41e-5 at levels 1 to 3, orders 1.153 and 1.093) is traced to a named term of the coupled step by a switch that brings its order to 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 4, or is shown to reach order 1.7 on finer levels or at a later time, or the ADR names why not with a number.
  - gap: On the full RL levels the order of R_b is still below 1.7 (1.198, 1.068, 1.598, 1.469). Only with the opt-in prescribed fringe flux (ADR 0347) is it 1.962, 1.789 on RE and 2.704, 2.124 within parity families. Not shown: when it reaches 1.7 without the opt-in, a formula for R_b; the alternation check (1.621 against 1.8) is a known miss.
  - note: From ADR 0246 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0340, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change. No clause of the order check is met. R_b (the library's quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on the background fringe against the default stencils; within 2.5 percent of ADR 0246) is 4.996e-5, 2.177e-5, 1.412e-5, 8.917e-6, 6.425e-6 at t = 0.5 on levels 1 to 5, orders 1.198, 1.068, 1.598, 1.469; run on to t = 3 on levels 1 to 3 it is 1.403e-4, 5.250e-5, 3.376e-5, orders 1.418, 1.089, and still growing; half the time step changes it by under 1 percent. Found on the way: the truncation of the background fringe of RL alternates between odd and even levels (coefficient 0.0685, 0.0781, 0.0621, 0.0693, 0.0638; the reflection of the fringe phase is not a symmetry), so orders between successive levels of RL carry a factor 1.26; within the parity families R_b has 1.150, 1.288, 1.542. On a set-up locked exactly, with equal spacings and no modulation along the ring (RE), the truncation converges at 1.995, 1.956 and R_b at 0.983, 1.015: the response per unit of truncation is proportional to the level (0.168, 0.339, 0.497) with no levelling off. Ruled out with numbers: a time-step or splitting term, a late settling at second order, the unequal spacings and the modulation. Named and confirmed: the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed softly. The flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is that of the pressure equation with the interpolated fringe pressure and differs from the face-interpolated velocity by a defect D held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D (measured face by face on RE: 0.9986, 1.0162 of that, correlation 0.995, 0.999), a resistance proportional to nu / h. The calculated cell across a fringe face follows a change of the normal fringe velocity by 0.51, 0.66, 0.76, 0.79, 0.83 at the background fringe (levels 1 to 5, t = 0.5; 0.10 to 0.51 at t = 0.025) and by 0.34 to 0.83 at the component fringe; each fringe costs about half an order on these levels. Refining the background alone raises R_b. Not shown: the level or time at which R_b reaches 1.7, and a formula for R_b from the resistance. One registered kinematic check missed (the truncation order between levels 3 and 4, 1.621 against 1.8, the alternation) and is kept as a known miss. Controls held, five mutations caught. Follow-up (ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): an opt-in that prescribes the flux of the calculated-fringe faces from the interpolated velocity. ADR 0347 (F-445), 2026-11-12: with the flux of the fringe faces prescribed and the pressure gradient of the neighbouring calculated cells taken from their own part, the order of R_b is 1.962, 1.789 on RE and 2.704, 2.124 within the parity families of RL: removing the soft imposition named here restores the order. The response is then larger on the levels run (R_b 9.0 to 3.3 times), because the interpolation error is handed on in full.
- [~] **F-350** Strong body-flow coupling selectable from the case tree
  - depends on: F-251
  - acceptance: A case with dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling = "strong" (default "loose") and its relaxation, added-mass estimate, tolerance, force scale and iteration cap as keys runs the spring-mounted piston at a mass ratio of 4 through the case driver and reproduces ADR 0250 S1 to S3 (omega within 2 percent, no growth of same-side turning points over 10 periods, dt halving within 0.5 percent), the same case with coupling = "loose" stops with a located error or grows; a step that reaches the cap stops the run with a located message unless a key says to continue; every static check of the new keys is located; with the default every existing case hash is bit-identical.
  - gap: Done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0349 Q1 recommends done). Open ADR 0266 questions: Q1 status, Q3 Newmark, Q4 rest patches. The wall pressure of the body force stays the default extrapolation (F-358).
  - note: From ADR 0250 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. PARTIAL (ADR 0266, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment): the optional table [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling] (absent from every case that does not write it; a key inside the existing table six_dof would need an entry in the H1 hash table, so the acceptance's coupling = "strong" is written scheme = "strong" in that table) selects the strong coupling of rcfd_fv::fsi::strong_step in the case driver; keys scheme (loose default, strong), relaxation (aitken default, fixed), added_mass (the factor 2M/(2M + m')), tolerance, force_scale, moment_scale, max_iterations, at_cap (stop default, continue). Tree runs equal strong_step called directly bit for bit (60 steps with ADR 0250's settings, 40 with a fixed factor and every key away from its default). The spring-mounted piston of ADR 0250 at mass ratio 4 through the case driver gives ADR 0250's numbers to their printed digits: omega_m/omega 1.005081 at T/100 (limit 2 %), dt halving 1.7e-5 (limit 0.5 %), largest ratio of same-side turning points 0.92452 and 0.96141 over 11 crossings (never grows), 3.0 flow solves a step; with scheme = "loose" (or no table) it passes 10 X at step 28 (T/100) and 31 (T/200) and stops at steps 34 and 40 with a located mesh error. A step at the cap stops the run with "dynamic_mesh: step N, t = ...: dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling.max_iterations: ..."; with at_cap = "continue" the run goes on with one warning event, and the cap 1 equals the loose run bit for bit. Every static check of the new keys is located at its key (strong with a prescribed motion, rest patches or Newmark; tolerance, scales, added mass, cap; unknown values and keys). Without the table nothing changes: baseline hashes, case_hashes_w48u, the K0 tests of ADR 0257 and 0262 and the dynamic_mesh tree tests pass unedited; a table with scheme = "loose" equals no table bit for bit. The one mutation of ADR 0266 that passed its named test (force_scale not read; the floor k X was inert in E1 because moment_scale = 0 makes the moment term the unfloored force ratio) is caught by the binding-floor test of ADR 0349 (F-437, 2026-11-12); proposed done by ADR 0349 Q1. Done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0349 Q1 recommends done). Open: ADR 0266 Q1 (status), Q2 (the key name), Q3 (Newmark), Q4 (rest patches). The wall pressure of the body force stays the default extrapolation (F-358). Follow-up: F-437. The key naming (Q2: scheme = "strong" in the table [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling]) accepted by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12. Maintainer (2026-11-18): the open questions above that were listed before the standing instruction of 2026-11-11 are closed by the lead on their written recommendations, except any that would change a default result, a golden or a hash table or that needs a source; those stay as they are. Status check (2026-11-18, by Claude from the text of ADR 0266; no test was run again): stays PARTIAL, and not only by the status rule of 2026-11-13: one mutation (MU5) is caught only by a test of another record (ADR 0349), and ADR 0266 Q1, Q3 and Q4 are open.
- [x] **F-351** Wall pressure of the body force on a fixed-flux moving wall (the 1.25 percent added-mass deficit)
  - depends on: F-251, F-244
  - acceptance: The cause of the discrete added mass of the piston column lying 1.25 percent below rho A L0 (ADR 0250 C1 and S1, ADR 0211 B1) is identified by a test that separates the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment from the pressure of the flow step; if it is the extrapolation, an opt-in evaluation that uses the prescribed pressure gradient of the wall brings the sub-iteration gain at ratio 4 within 0.2 percent of the 2.977 of the model and omega_m/omega within 0.1 percent of 1 on the 20-cell column, and the convergence of the deficit with the cell size is shown on 20, 40 and 80 cells; the default force evaluation is unchanged unless the maintainer approves the change with its effect on the existing hashes listed.
  - note: DONE, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0250 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0252, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, four amendments). Cause, measured: the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment. Its least-squares gradient (weights 1/d^2) takes the stored zero-gradient wall value of the pressure field as a data point with the weight of the neighbour cell, while the pressure equation of the moving-mesh step used the prescribed gradient -n . a_wall; the gradient of the wall cell is therefore exactly half (0.5 to 1e-16) and the wall pressure a quarter cell short: the force is low by 1/(4N), first order in the cell size (prescribed piston, flow step converged: 1.2510e-2, 6.258e-3, 3.129e-3 on 20, 40, 80 cells, orders 0.9993 and 0.9998), 1.25 percent on the 20-cell column at every mass ratio. The pressure of the flow step carries none of it (2e-6 with the step converged, 7e-6 with the registered two correctors). Delivered, opt-in, nothing calls it: sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient (the normal part of the cell-gradient extrapolation replaced by the gradient of ale::set_follow_conditions, p_c + dn g on an orthogonal wall cell, second order) and fsi::strong_step_with with fsi::WallPressure, which carries that gradient from step to step. With it: gain of the sub-iteration at ratio 4 2.97693 (model 2.977, limit 0.2 percent); omega_m/omega 1.000042 at ratio 4 on 20, 40 and 80 cells (limit 0.1 percent; 1.005081, 1.002552, 1.001294 with the default), 0.999963 at ratio 20, 1.000068 at 0.2, 1.000264 for the loose loop at 0.2 (1.001307 before: the unexplained +1.0e-3 of ADR 0211 was this deficit); deficit of the force 3e-6 on 20, 40, 80 cells. Every number equals the piston model with the exact added mass to six digits. Unchanged: patch_force_moment and strong_step (bit-identical over 40 steps; the sixdof, sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244 and strong_fsi_f251 suites pass unedited; baseline_hashes 3 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the file unedited)); pimple.rs, pimple/moving.rs, rcfd-api and the case schema untouched. Seven library mutations: six failed their checks; one added variant passed every test and a check (the gain at the third step of a run) was added by amendment and catches it. Disclosed: the first registered diagnosis missed its limits because its reference was the column of the new mesh; the pressure of the implicit Euler moving-mesh step is the acceleration times the column of the old mesh (first order in dt, not a mean deficit), and the reference was corrected by amendment after an exploration; the missed tests are kept as ignored records. Also found: the non-iterated step leaves a viscous splitting error that grows with the cell count and does not move the frequency. Not delivered: the case driver (rcfd-api dynmesh) still uses the default evaluation; a skewed wall cell and a moment in a flow are not tested. Open, the maintainer's: whether the prescribed gradient becomes the default (ADR 0252 Q1; not taken, it moves existing results), the case key (Q2), the audit of other walls with a prescribed gradient (Q3). Note of the lead: the acceptance limits were never changed, but the limits of the diagnosis were corrected by amendment 2 after a run and a prints-only exploration, so they were set with numbers seen. Follow-up (ADR 0252 questions 1 to 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-358. Open: question 1 (the prescribed gradient as the default changes existing hashes).
- [x] **F-352** Overset: donor search on cells with non-planar faces
  - depends on: F-134
  - acceptance: On the set-up B3d of ADR 0251 (two hexahedral parts whose interior points are displaced by up to 0.15 of the cell size in all three directions) every fringe centre gets a donor that agrees with a full search, the linear and the quadratic stencils reproduce linear and quadratic fields to 1e-11, and on meshes with planar faces the donors and stencils are bit-identical to those of today (the unit tests K2 and K4 of ADR 0219 and D1 of ADR 0251).
  - note: DONE, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0253, 2026-11-12: DONE. Derived: one plane for each face leaves no gap across a face but a sliver along every edge at which the planes of the four faces do not meet in one line, a gap or an overlap with equal chance, of cross-section at most (w_F + w_F')(w_G + w_G') for the warps w of the faces, second order in the warp; on B3d (warp up to 0.142 of the cell size) the estimate was 6e-4 of the volume each and 116 and 114 of 200000 random points were measured in no cell and in two. Built in rcfd_mesh::overset: a cell with a face warped beyond the locator's tolerance (1e-10 of its box diagonal) is tested as the polyhedron of the triangles about its face centres, the same triangles from both sides of a face (triangulated_margin: the distance from the triangles, signed by the winding number, behind a bounding-box shortcut); a cell with planar faces keeps the plane test of ADR 0219 M3 unchanged; a point on a shared triangle goes to the lowest-numbered cell. Met: on B3d all 1069 fringe centres get a donor equal to the full search and confirmed by an independent tetrahedral test, the linear stencils reproduce a linear field to 3e-16 and the quadratic stencils q3 to 9e-16 with no fallback; 250000 random points in the two warped parts each lie in exactly one cell; 39744 face centres and 12167 mesh points go to the lowest-numbered cell; on the planar set-ups (RL, TG_L, U, TR, DC, FB, B3, B3s) no cell is warped and the donors and default stencils equal those built from the rule of M3 bit for bit; K2, K4, D1, Q0 and the records R2 pass unedited. Cost: a search takes 4.5 microseconds on B3d, the connectivity 1.8 times that of B3. The present rule finds no cell for the fringe cells 16035 (as recorded) and 16245. Six mutations caught. Limits: kinematic only, one family of warped meshes; non-convex cells with planar faces keep the plane test. Open for the maintainer: whether every cell should use the triangulated test (it changes one donor of TR at a tie, ADR 0253 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0253 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-356, F-357. Open: question 1 (the triangulated test for every cell changes one donor at a tie).
- [x] **F-353** Overset: the moving cylinder with the quadratic donor interpolation
  - depends on: F-336
  - acceptance: The set-up TR of ADR 0219 run with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic: mass of the domain and continuity within 1e-9, no fallback or the count reported, drag within 5 percent of the body-fitted run at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 and the difference to the linear-stencil run reported; the ADR recommends for or against making the quadratic interpolation the default.
  - note: DONE, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0259, 2026-11-12: DONE (tests and ADR only, no library change). The set-up TR of ADR 0219 with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic over 400 steps: continuity 5.6e-17, net outflow 9.4e-15 of U D L, no fallback (156 stencils of nine cells at every step), no unconverged solve, drag within 5.86e-3 of the body-fitted run at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 (linear stencils 6.25e-3; the linear run and the body-fitted run reproduce ADR 0219 to every printed digit). Against the linear run: C_D lower by 2.1e-4 on average (largest 1.6e-3), mean drag error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3, worse by more than 1e-4 at 164 of 301 steps; the step-to-step drag oscillation as the body crosses background cells halves (rms 0.98e-3 against 1.80e-3 of C_D); time 1.03 times. By the rule fixed before the run the ADR recommends against making the quadratic interpolation the default; the default stays the maintainer's decision (ADR 0259 Q1). Three mutations caught by the fast test.
- [~] **F-354** Immersed solid: DFG 2D-2 force extrema, mesh and time-step convergence
  - depends on: F-346
  - acceptance: DFG 2D-2 with the immersed cylinder is run on the T mesh and on T refined once (D/80, half the time step) and on M2 and M3; the maximum drag and lift on the finest mesh are within 1.5 percent of the FeatFlow level-6 values and the error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on both families, or the part that does not converge (mesh of the wake, forcing order, outlet condition, time step) is identified by a registered measurement.
  - gap: Missing: on the M family with build, the lift error does not decrease from D/40 to D/80 (0.161 to 0.283, a known miss). Open: ADR 0268 Q5 (the stop), Q6 (quote the D/80 values as the validation), Q7 (status).
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0268, 2026-11-12), measurement only, no library code. From ADR 0249 question 5. DFG 2D-2 with the immersed cylinder was run to t = 8 on T and on T refined once (T2, D/80, dt 5e-4) and on M2 and M3 (M3 also at dt 5e-4), with `build` and with `build_second_order_bounded`, against the FeatFlow level-6 values. On the D/80 meshes max C_D and max C_L are within 0.43 percent with either forcing (T2 build +0.272/+0.325, T2 bounded +0.136/+0.175, M3 build +0.143/-0.283, M3 bounded +0.007/-0.429; St within 0.13 percent). The error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on the T family with build (lift 2.580 to 0.325), on the M family with the bounded form (1.011 to 0.429), and on the M family with build in the drag (0.261 to 0.143) but not in the lift (0.161 to 0.283, a known miss accounted for by the part measurements). Part measurements, each registered with its decision numbers: refining only the core around the cylinder on T takes the lift error from +2.69 to +0.02 percent, so the mesh at the cylinder carries the T anomaly; the rest of the mesh then moves it 0.31 point, halving the time step 0.11 (T) and 0.04 (M2) point, and moving the outlet from x = 2.2 to 4.4 changes nothing to six digits; the T and M families differ by 2.74 points of lift at D/40 and by 0.61 at D/80, so the M2 agreement of ADR 0249 was a cancellation between the D/40 core and the coarse outer mesh; the forcing order moves the extrema by up to 1.17 points at D/40 (M2) and at most 0.15 at D/80. Missing (why partial): T with the bounded forcing (D/40) stopped at step 2951 by the divergence guard, with pressure NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell, so the decrease on the T family with the bounded form is not formed; not diagnosed (library work). Open: ADR 0268 Q5 (the stop), Q6 (quote the D/80 values as the validation), Q7 (status). ADR 0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of T with the bounded form was a breakdown of the AMG-preconditioned pressure CG at step 2951 (r^T z < 0, finite inputs); with the opt-in pressure_ic_fallback T runs to t = 8, max C_D +0.216 and max C_L +1.687 percent, so A2-T-2 is met (0.216 to 0.136, 1.687 to 0.175) and the forcing order on T moves the extrema by -0.60 and -0.89 point. Maintainer (2026-11-18): the open questions above that were listed before the standing instruction of 2026-11-11 are closed by the lead on their written recommendations, except any that would change a default result, a golden or a hash table or that needs a source; those stay as they are.
- [~] **F-355** Second-order immersed forcing: transient PISO at Re 100
  - depends on: F-309
  - acceptance: DFG 2D-2 on M2 with `build_second_order` runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2 and gives a Strouhal number within 1 percent of the first-order forcing on the same mesh, or the cause of the stop at step 6 is diagnosed by a registered measurement and the configuration is refused with a located message.
  - gap: The first branch is met only with the bounded opt-in, not with build_second_order as named. Known misses: flux velocity after step 1 is 2.49 against 4.5; the bounded form with one corrector stops at step 34 (unexplained, depends on the time step). Open ADR 0254 Q1 to Q3: whether build_second_order builds the bounded form (F-364), the form of the refusal, the single corrector.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0254, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0249 question 6. The stop was reproduced (step 6, Courant 1.1094e7) and diagnosed by registered variant runs, each with its first-order control: it needs a fluid-solid face whose surface crossing lies close to the fluid cell centre, so that the linear extension of ADR 0234 D1 has a weight above 5 (it multiplies the velocity of the first fluid cell relative to the wall by up to 38 on M2), together with the impulsive start; runs with weights of at most 5 (theta_min 0.1, 0.25, 0.5; mesh M1) and a run started from a developed field do not stop, and at each of the five steps the largest flux velocity sits on the face of weight 38.99 (2.49, 23, 1426, 9.2e4, 6.9e5). Ruled out, each by its number: the ddt flux correction, the corrector count, BDF2, the convection scheme, the time step (5e-4 to 8e-3 all stop) and the continuity of the fluid cells (7e-7). A hand estimate of a linear growth criterion (weight times the share of the time term in the diagonal) was refuted by its registered rule. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::build_second_order_bounded` (opt-in): on the faces with a weight above 2 the flux is that of the wall value reflected through the image point of the face in the fluid, interpolated between the first fluid cell and the cell behind it, weights of magnitude at most 1, second order; `build` and `build_second_order` are bit-identical (three hashes, the existing immersed tests, baseline_hashes). With it DFG 2D-2 on M2 runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2: Strouhal number 0.30112 against 0.30041 of the first-order forcing (+0.24 percent, limit 1), C_D max -0.33 percent and C_L max -1.01 percent of FeatFlow; circular Couette error 5.91e-3, 1.63e-3, 4.23e-4, order 1.947 (limit 1.5), PISO equal to SIMPLEC to 0.1 percent. `build_second_order` itself is refused by PimpleSolver with a located message where a flux face has a weight above 5 and can return more than the time term carries (`flux_growth`; 2D-2 on M2 at step 1, value 2.2; the runs of ADR 0234 and 0249 are not refused); the refusal is a sufficient condition, not a stability criterion (time steps of 4e-3 and 8e-3 still stop by the Courant guard). Seven mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule because of two known misses: the flux velocity after the first step was registered as at least 4.5 and is 2.49 (the growth builds over steps 2 to 5), and the bounded form with a single PISO corrector stops at step 34 (any flux face that returns the wall-normal velocity at full size does, with one corrector; with two or more it runs). Acceptance: the second branch (diagnosis and located refusal) is met; the first is met with the bounded opt-in, not with `build_second_order` as named. Open (ADR 0254 questions 1 to 3): whether `build_second_order` should build the bounded form (changes recorded numbers of ADR 0234 and 0239), the form of the refusal, the single corrector. Not run: M3, T, three dimensions, PIMPLE outer iterations, SIMPLE with under-relaxation. Follow-ups: F-363 (the single corrector), F-364 (the bounded form as build_second_order; needs the maintainer). ADR 0268 (2026-11-12, F-354): `build_second_order_bounded` ran 2D-2 to t = 8 on T2 and M3 (D/80, within 0.43 percent of FeatFlow) but stopped on T (D/40, dt 1e-3) at step 2951, with pressure NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell; not diagnosed. ADR 0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of build_second_order_bounded on T (ADR 0268) is not a stop of the forcing but of the AMG-preconditioned pressure CG (r^T z < 0 at step 2951); with the opt-in PimpleSettings::pressure_ic_fallback the run reaches t = 8. - [x] **F-360** Co-simulation protocol over the solver service
  - depends on: F-139, F-085
  - acceptance: The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md (describe, time, checkpoint, restore, forces, advance) are served by the JSON-RPC service under a new protocol version; an out-of-process mock structural participant driven over TCP reproduces ADR 0256 A1 and A2 (every step converged, omega_m/omega within 0.5 percent and 3 percent) and the same displacements as the in-process run to 1e-12; a dropped connection or a participant error stops the step with a located error and both sides restored; the protocol document is versioned; existing service tests and case hashes are unchanged.
  - note: Merged 2026-11-12. DONE (ADR 0345, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, two amendments). The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md are served by the JSON-RPC service for participants that the embedding program hosts (rcfd_api::cosim_service: Service::host_fluid, host_structure, each participant on its own thread so it need not be Send; rcfd serve hosts none; no case key, CLI or MCP change): methods cosim.list, cosim.open, cosim.describe, cosim.time, cosim.checkpoint, cosim.restore, cosim.forces, cosim.advance, plain JSON numbers that cross bit for bit (serde_json float_roundtrip), error codes 1005 (the participant error, its own message) and 1006 (no such participant). Service protocol 1.1: the identifier rcfd-service/1 is kept (the pinned tests are unedited), service.info gains protocol_version 1.1 and cosim rcfd-cosim/1; both protocol pages are versioned. The coupler is the unchanged cosim::coupled_step driven with the proxies RemoteStructure and RemoteFluid (TCP). A lease per participant (cosim.open) refuses requests left over from an old connection; a proxy whose connection is lost fails at once except restore, which reconnects once and restores the participant, so a dropped connection ends the step with the located error and both sides at the start of the step. Measured on the model problem of ADR 0256 with the mock structure in a second process: every one of 650 steps converged, 7 to 10 iterations (mean 8.766), omega_m/omega 0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every node at every step equal to the in-process run bit for bit (limit 1e-12 X), also with both participants remote (100 steps); a participant error (structure in the other process, fluid hosted) and a dropped connection (cut before the request, after the reply, between steps, fluid or structure) each give an error naming participant, time and iteration with 0 bits of either state changed and the next step equal to the reference; a killed participant process gives the located error in 2.1 s with the fluid restored and the failed reconnection reported; refusals with their codes; a control with springs stiffer by 1e-9 is seen (4e-9 X). Amendment 1: the first transport cost 2 ms per call (lines written in pieces), now 0.05 ms (one write per line, TCP_NODELAY on accepted connections; no byte changes). Amendment 2: the 650-step out-of-process tests are ignored heavy records (minutes on the loaded machine; run twice, identical), the gate runs the 100-step both-remote comparison and the failure tests. Existing service, CLI and MCP suites and the case hashes pass unedited; seven mutations each failed their tests. Not delivered: participants built from a case or hosted by rcfd serve, structural elements in describe, authentication, a test of a call outlasting the time-out. Open: ADR 0345 Q1 to Q5. Follow-up F-444 (ADR 0380, 2026-11-12): participants from the case hosted by rcfd serve --cosim, elements in describe, one write per service::Client request (ADR 0345 Q3, Q4, Q5).
- [x] **F-361** Quasi-Newton acceleration of the coupled iteration
  - depends on: F-139
  - acceptance: A least-squares (quasi-Newton) update of the nodal force from the residual history of the step, opt-in beside the fixed and Aitken factors, converges the model problem of ADR 0256 to 1e-8 in at most 7 iterations per step and 6 or fewer on average (Aitken: 8.8), gives the same frequencies within 1e-6, and with one rigid node needs no more iterations than Aitken; registered before the run with the plain fixed point as the diverging control.
  - note: DONE (ADR 0261, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, no amendment). Opt-in fsi::Relaxation::LeastSquares { initial, filter } (CouplingSettings::least_squares) in cosim::coupled_step: after a first update relaxed with initial, the next nodal force is the flow's force plus the combination of the step's output differences whose residual differences best cancel the current residual (interface quasi-Newton with a least-squares inverse Jacobian), solved by Householder QR newest column first with a filter that drops a column whose part outside the newer ones is below 1e-2 of its norm (no vanishing pivot); no reuse across steps; fsi::strong_step refuses it. Derived: on a linear map it is GMRES plus one pass, exact at iteration d + 2. Measured on the model problem of ADR 0256 (6 nodes, 16 faces, tolerance 1e-8): every one of 650 steps converged, at most 7 iterations (one step), mean 5.980 (Aitken 8.766, histogram identical to ADR 0256), frequencies equal to Aitken's within 3.1e-10; one rigid node (SPm1): the same 301 iterations as Aitken, the same count in every step, positions bit-identical; the plain fixed point diverges (510.85 in 10). Mock affine and cubic fluids check the termination count and the equality with Aitken's secant. Existing suites cosim_f139, strong_fsi_f251, added_mass_f351 and the baseline hashes pass unedited; four mutations caught. Open: ADR 0261 Q1 to Q3.
- [x] **F-362** Interface mapping by geometric search and radial-basis functions, with an unmapped-value policy
  - depends on: F-139
  - acceptance: InterfaceMap weights are built from the two interface meshes alone (nearest-element projection and a radial-basis interpolation) for a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes; rigid translation and rotation are reproduced to 1e-12, resultant force, moment and work are conserved to 1e-12 by the transposed map, a wall point outside the structure is refused or mapped by a stated policy, and the model problem of ADR 0256 gives the same frequencies within 1e-3 with the built weights.
  - note: DONE; the entry below was written while the item was partial, and the decision is recorded later in this note. First recorded as partial (ADR 0263, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment after the registered run). Opt-in cosim::interface_rows and InterfaceMap::build build the weights from the structure's nodes and elements (points, segments, triangles, quadrilaterals) and the fluid's wall points alone; nothing calls them. Derived: scalar weights reproduce every rigid motion iff each row sums to 1 and reproduces the point's coordinates; the transpose then conserves resultant and moment, and conserves work for any weights. Nearest-element projection with an offset correction on the ring of elements (exact on a curved wall; plain barycentric selectable); radial basis with Wendland's C2 function of support 3 h and a degree-1 polynomial in the nodes' own directions, dense Cholesky with a Schur complement, condition estimate (8 to 85 here). Policy: a wall point farther than max_distance is refused (the default; the message names point and distance) or moves with its nearest structural point (Unmapped::Nearest). Measured on a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes: rigid translation and rotation to 1.3e-15, resultant, moment and work to 1.4e-16 (both methods); without the correction the cylinder loses 5e-3 of the rotation and 1e-4 of the moment; outside points follow their nearest points to 9e-16 and the moment changes exactly as predicted. Model problem of ADR 0256: the projection gives the piecewise-linear rows to 1e-16 and the same frequencies (1.4e-15); the radial basis shifts them by -5.2e-4 and +1.9e-4 (limit 1e-3). cosim_f139, cosim_f361 and the baseline hashes pass unedited; eight mutations caught. Partial because the registered check E1 accepted two coincident nodes with the radial basis (an absolute pivot test); amendment 1 refuses pivots below 2 n eps a_jj, and E1b passes with it. Protocol option in docs/cosimulation-protocol.md. Open: ADR 0263 Q1 to Q3. ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).

ADR 0392 (2026-11-13, F-482): a finite-difference linearisation of the whole step finds the period-two mode of the bounded form with one corrector at dt 1e-3 (-1.10 +- 0.35i at step 15, -1.27 at step 10, at the body) and every Ritz value inside the unit circle at dt 5e-4 and with two correctors; with one corrector at dt 1e-3 both forcings also have positive pressure modes up to 1.9, so the one-step spectrum does not separate the setting that stops from the first-order forcing that runs. Periodic steady identity on ADR 0223's periodic channel (velocity 1e-10 U0; mean-removed pressure against max(1e-10, 2x the default's own drift) of the range): non-orthogonal correctors on a 26.6-degree shear 1.5e-12 U0 and 7.1e-11; face jumps 2.1e-12 and 4.2e-11 (also from the hook); the component diagonal 3.9e-12 and 5.2e-10 (drift 5.6e-10); all three together 1.4e-12 and 1.2e-11; ADR 0223's E2 alone passes the same limit (2.5e-10 against 6.6e-10). Transients differ from the default by 2e-6 to 2e-5 U0 at dt 0.001. The other rows stay refused with their located messages (moving mesh, gradient options, periodic faces without the periodic flag). Nine mutations caught. Defaults bit-identical (seven fingerprints recorded on 2ad9dcb9, the rcfd-fv transient suites, baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u). Why partial: the registered set-up checks of the component-diagonal and all-together channels missed (3000 steps do not reach a steady state with a symmetry plane, whose start-up decays at nu (pi/2H)^2); their identities were met only after amendment 1 (8000 steps). The opt-in is not yet folded into ConsistentCorrectors (ADR 0360 Q1) and there is no case key.

N = 12, Hex20: supported ring and clamped disc, every harmonic 0 to 6, frequencies equal to the full 360-degree model within 4.0e-14 and 1.8e-13 (limit 1e-8) with equal counts below the cut-off (36, 23), pair splits 2.8e-13, expanded-mode residual 8.2e-12 (limit 1e-7) and M-orthonormality 2.3e-15; thin ring t/R = 0.05, nu = 0: n = 2 at k = 2 within 4.4e-4, n = 3 at k = 3 within 1.8e-3 (limit 2 percent); spinning annular disc b/a = 4, nu = 0.3: rim displacement within 8.9e-5 of rho omega^2 b ((3 + nu) a^2 + (1 - nu) b^2)/(4E) (derived; agrees with the roadmap; limit 1 percent), sector statics equal to the full disc within 3.3e-13. Refusals: unmatched boundaries with the first unmatched node, N < 2, k > N/2. Eight mutations caught. si_scaffold x1/r1-r9/r10 after landed and si_mpc N5 kept as ignored records (maintainer decision 2026-11-13). Open, taken on the standing instruction: modal_analysis and solve_static on a model with a Cyclic constraint give the k = 0 result (documented). Follow-up F-489 (harmonic loads, rigid sets at k > 0).
- [~] **F-395** Geometric (initial-stress) stiffness of solid elements: pre-stressed modal analysis and linear buckling
  - depends on: F-388, F-374, F-376, F-382, F-383
  - milestones: fan-structure
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. K_sigma is symmetric within 1e-13 of its norm, gives no force for a rigid translation within 1e-12, and for a uniform uniaxial stress s and a linear displacement field w gives x^T K_sigma x = s V |grad w . e|^2 within 1e-12. rcfd-linalg: for K = tridiagonal (2, -1), n = 200, and K_sigma = -I the ten lowest buckling factors equal 4 sin^2(j pi/(2 (n + 1))) within 1e-10; a K_sigma with no negative direction returns no factor and says so. Pre-stressed modes: a beam on knife-edge supports at its neutral axis (slenderness 20, nu = 0) under an axial tension stress s has (omega_n^2 - omega_n,0^2) = (n pi/L)^2 s/rho within 1 percent for n = 1 and 2, and under compression the frequency falls by the same amount. Buckling: the same beam in compression has the critical load pi^2 E I/L^2 reduced by the shear term (0.6 percent at this slenderness, registered) within 1 percent, the second factor four times the first within 2 percent; a clamped-free column pi^2 E I/(4 L^2) within 1 percent (Tet10 or Hex20).
  - gap: The second buckling factor is 2.0135e-2 from four times the first against the limit 2e-2, because the solid's K_sigma carries axial stress on rotating sections. The note says a follow-up settled this against a derived closed form (1.7e-4) and at L/h = 40 (0.52 percent), but not against the acceptance as written. The transformation path is refused.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). ADR 0390, 2026-11-13: geometric stiffness of Tet4, Hex8, Tet10 and Hex20 (geometric::element_geometric_stiffness, Prestress from a static result, geometric_stiffness on the stiffness pattern, bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads), pre-stressed modes (geometric::prestressed_modes; a zero pre-stress has the bits of modal_analysis) and linear buckling (buckling::factors on rcfd_linalg::eigen::lowest_buckling_factors, subspace iteration on K^-1 (-K_sigma) verified by a Sturm count of K + s K_sigma; with no factor it returns the bound below which there is none). Symmetry 2.0e-16, translation 2.5e-16, uniaxial form 5.3e-15; tridiagonal factors 4.4e-15; frequency shifts 6.8e-4 and 2.4e-3 (tension), 5.0e-4 and 2.2e-3 (compression); knife-edge buckling 2.0e-3 from Engesser (shear term 0.491 percent registered); clamped-free column 1.7e-3. Known miss: the second factor is 2.0135e-2 from four times the first against 2e-2, because the solid's K_sigma also carries the axial stress on the rotating sections (r^2 k^2, the order of the shear term; the derived form matches within 1.7e-4). Transformation path (springs, linear constraints, rigid sets) refused. Follow-ups F-492 (the knife-edge factors against the derived closed form), F-493 (transformation path). The A9 clause is settled by F-492 (ADR 0394): the solid's factors match the derived closed form within 1.7e-4, and at L/h = 40 the second factor is four times the first within 0.52 percent.
- [~] **F-396** Modes of a rotating part: stress stiffening by the centrifugal pre-stress, spin softening, Campbell diagram
  - depends on: F-395, F-375, F-383
  - milestones: fan-structure
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At zero speed the result has the bits of the modal analysis of F-383. Radial bar clamped on the axis, nu = 0, axial modes: (omega_n,0^2 - omega_n^2)/Omega^2 = 1 within 1e-3 for n = 1, 2 at a speed with centrifugal stress below 1e-4 E. Radial beam of square section clamped on the axis (slenderness 20): the first out-of-plane (flap) and in-plane (lag) frequencies satisfy omega_flap^2 - omega_lag^2 = Omega^2 within 1e-4 Omega^2 on a symmetric mesh; the stiffening (omega_flap^2 - omega_0^2)/Omega^2 equals at Omega = 0.2 omega_0 the Rayleigh quotient of the centrifugal tension with the mode at rest (1.19, recomputed in the registration) within 2 percent and stays between 1 and that value up to Omega = 5 omega_0. Campbell table: on a synthetic family omega^2 = omega_0^2 + S Omega^2 the crossings with orders 1 to 4 equal omega_0/sqrt(k^2 - S) within 1e-8, and on the beam within 1 percent; a flap and a lag mode of a rectangular section that cross are tracked without exchange (modal assurance above 0.9). Radial bar: spin softening 1 within 1.9e-9, the full operator 1 - Q_n,h within 3.1e-5; square beam: stiffening 1.1907 at 0.2 omega_0 (2.2e-3 from 1.1933), between 1 and the rest quotient up to 5 omega_0, crossings within 8.7e-6 of direct solves; flap and lag of a rectangular section tracked through their crossing (MAC 0.99999). Partial: the flap-lag identity misses 1e-4 at 1.9e-3 (known miss, predicted in the registration): on a solid it is 1 - 2 f_x (met to 1.1e-8), f_x the axial kinetic share of the bending mode. Coriolis neglected. Follow-ups: the flap-lag clause restated for a solid, Coriolis coupling, rotating modes of a sector at a harmonic index. Follow-ups F-498 (flap-lag restated for a solid), F-499 (Coriolis), F-500 (cyclic sector at a harmonic index).

  - depends on: F-388, F-373, F-374, F-383
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Free vibration started in the first axial mode of a bar (the discrete eigenvector): with Newmark the amplitude after 100 periods is within 1e-9 and the total energy constant within 1e-10; the measured period is long by (omega dt)^2/12 within 5 percent of that amount at omega dt = 0.2 and 0.1, observed order >= 1.9. A step load proportional to M phi_1 gives the peak displacement twice the static one within 0.5 percent at 40 steps per period. Bar of 20 Hex8: amplitude after 100 periods 9e-15, energy 2.5e-14, period error 0.9974 and 0.9993 of (omega dt)^2/12, order 1.997; step-load peak 1.0e-5 from twice static; Rayleigh 0.02 decrement 1.7e-3; rho_inf = 1 equals Newmark to 1.6e-14; split run and 1/8 threads bit-equal; the three refusals and 16 more. - [~] **F-400** Dynamic solid as a co-simulation participant, on interface weights built from the two surfaces
  - depends on: F-398, F-139, F-361, F-362, F-385
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A bar (nu = 0) whose end face is the interface, coupled by coupled_step to a mock fluid that returns the force -m_a times the wall acceleration: the first coupled frequency equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho A L/m_a within 1 percent at 100 steps per period, for mass ratios m_a/(rho A L) of 0.5 and 4; at ratio 4 the plain iteration (factor 1) diverges as the protocol predicts (registered control) while Aitken's factor and the least-squares update converge to 1e-8 within registered iteration caps. With a mock spring k_f and a slow load the response tends to F_0/(k_s + k_f) of F-385 within 1e-6. Mapping built by F-362 for a matching and for a 3:2 non-matching interface: resultant force, moment and work conserved within 1e-12, and the coupled frequency changes by less than 1e-3 between the two. Restore returns the checkpoint bit for bit; a failing structural step stops the coupled step with the participant's name and both sides restored. No flow solver is coupled.
  - gap: The coupled frequency change between the matching and the 3:2 map is 6.3e-3 (ratio 4) and 2.4e-3 (ratio 0.5) against the limit 1e-3. The cause is non-consistent weights in the transposed projection. A follow-up measures it by face refinement (below 1e-3 from 8 x 8 elements with the projection). ADR 0410 questions Q1 to Q3 remain open.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). PARTIAL (ADR 0410, 2026-11-13; registered before the code, amendment 1 after the registered run, amendment 2 after the mutations). rcfd_post::solid_dynamic::DynamicSolid implements cosim::Structure on the transient integrator of ADR 0389/0393 (Newmark or generalised-alpha, either path): advance holds the interface forces over one or more sub-steps through the new opt-in Integrator::run_with_force (the force added at both ends of every step, reduced like a load pattern; run and step keep their bits), checkpoint and restore keep the integrator's state and the held forces bit for bit, elements gives the surface set's faces to the map builders; no dependency edge added (rcfd-post already depends on rcfd-fv and rcfd-fem), rcfd-fv::cosim unchanged. Bar 4 x 1 x 1 m, Hex8 20 x 2 x 2, nu = 0, clamped, end face the interface, coupled by coupled_step to a test-only piston mock (one wall acceleration, Newmark-consistent, force -m_a a) at 100 steps per period: first coupled frequency against the root of k L tan(k L) = rho A L/m_a 2.8e-4 (ratio 0.5) and 3.3e-4 (ratio 4) (limit 1 %), against the discrete Newmark prediction 1.5e-7; the plain iteration diverges with the derived slope -m_a e^T S^{-1} e (-59.69 at ratio 4) to 6e-16; Aitken and least squares converge to 1e-8 in 3 iterations per step on the matching and the 3:2 map built by F-362; spring 1.5 k_s with a slow load (generalised-alpha rho_inf = 0) to F_0/(k_s + k_f) within 1.1e-10; resultant, moment and work conserved to 2.2e-16; restore bit for bit; a failing structural step (load table, non-finite force) stops the step naming 'solid' in iteration 1 and 2 with both sides restored. Partial: the coupled frequency changes by 6.3e-3 (ratio 4) and 2.4e-3 (ratio 0.5) between the matching and the 3:2 map (limit 1e-3; diagnosed: the transposed projection loads the 2 x 2 face with non-consistent weights, 1.5 % more static compliance; a known-miss record). The registered per-face added-mass mock made the coupled run unstable (non-uniform patterns with slopes of hundreds below the convergence test grow by about 700 per step); amendment 1 made the mock a piston. Eight mutations caught (one after amendment 2). Baseline hashes pass. No flow solver is coupled. Open: ADR 0410 Q1 to Q3. Follow-up: F-NEW (frequency change against the face refinement and the map). Follow-up F-502. The frequency change between the maps (M2c, 6.3e-3) is the extra static compliance of the mapped weights; its dependence on the face refinement and the map is measured by F-502 (ADR 0412, 2026-11-13): below 1e-3 from 8 x 8 elements with the projection and from 4 x 4 with the radial basis. The added-mass growth of the per-face mock (amendment 1) does not occur with the flow solver: in F-401 (ADR 0434, 2026-11-14) the non-uniform part of the interface force stays at rounding on the matching wall and decays on the 3:2 wall, its slopes being those of the local flow, far below 1. Maintainer (2026-11-18): the open questions above that were listed before the standing instruction of 2026-11-11 are closed by the lead on their written recommendations, except any that would change a default result, a golden or a hash table or that needs a source; those stay as they are.

Elastic bar (nu = 0) closing a channel of incompressible fluid of length L_f, started from a displaced state, mass ratios rho_f L_f/(rho_s L_s) of 0.5 and 4: the coupled iteration converges in every step to 1e-6 with Aitken's factor and with the least-squares update, iteration counts recorded; the frequency of the first coupled mode equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho_s L_s/(rho_f L_f) within 2 percent after the registered estimate of the time-step and viscous effects; over ten periods the work of the fluid on the interface equals the change of the solid's energy within 1e-4 of its amplitude; the loose coupling (one pass) at ratio 4 grows (registered control). Over 1001 steps at T/100: Aitken and the least-squares update converge to 1e-6 in 3 iterations every step on the matching wall and in 4 to 12 on a 3:2 wall (bilinear projection of F-504 on a 4 x 4 face); the first coupled frequency is the root of k L tan(k L) = rho_s L_s/(rho_f L_f) to 1.6e-4 (0.5) and 1.1e-3 (4), and the discrete model of the pairing (the Newmark bar with the plug force of the flow step, one step of lag: the registered time-step estimate) to 4e-7 (limit 2 percent after the estimate); over ten periods the fluid's work on the interface equals the change of the solid's energy to 5e-6 of its amplitude (limit 1e-4); the loose coupling at ratio 4 grows by 13.8 per step; the 3:2 wall changes the frequency by 8.2e-4 (4) and 3.1e-4 (0.5) (limit 2e-3; ADR 0414's piston mock gave 8.18e-4); a failing solid (load table) or fluid (mesh motion) stops the step naming it, both sides bit-equal to the start of the step. The non-uniform part of the interface force (ADR 0410 Q3) stays at 1e-9 of the force on the matching wall and decays over the run on the 3:2 wall (at most 8.8e-4): with a real column its slopes are far below 1, so the growth seen with F-400's per-face mock does not occur. Partial: the registered viscous estimate 0 is wrong in kind (the PISO step's viscous splitting moves the tip by 8.3e-5 U at nu x 100, proportional to nu; a known miss, below 1e-6 in frequency at the case's viscosity), and the helper check H1 was met only after amendment 1 (a limit below the coordinate's resolution). ADR 0446 (F-421, 2026-11-14) found that Symmetry planes add a dissipation to a flow tangential to them in the PISO step (+7 to +13 percent of the viscous impedance of an oscillating channel); this may be the cause of the VS miss of ADR 0434 (not tested). ADR 0344, 2026-11-12: the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY with a new opt-in frame. Limits: the lab memory is derived for translation along a planar layer; matched forms on rotating meshes are not built; library only; two-dimensional checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the registered check G3 missed (a defect of its set-up, 8.92e-3 against 1e-12) and passed only as G3b after amendment 1, which is not blind to the scratch model that explained the miss; done is the maintainer's call. The complex modulus function returns E' = E_inf + sum E_i w^2 tau_i^2/(1 + w^2 tau_i^2) and E'' = sum E_i w tau_i/(1 + w^2 tau_i^2) within 1e-13, and a strain cycled in time dissipates pi eps0^2 E'' per cycle and volume within 1 percent at 200 steps per cycle. ADR 0485, 2026-11-14 (registration of stub ADR 0313): linear viscoelasticity in rcfd-fem (mat_visco.rs). The generalised Maxwell solid on an isotropic base, with shear and bulk weights per Prony term and the recursive update of the internal stresses, exact for a strain linear in the step, and its tangent. The state is 6 (N + 1) values per point: the strain of the last step and one internal stress per term. The WLF and Arrhenius shifts act through the reduced time. complex_moduli gives the shear, bulk and Young's complex moduli; modulus_table builds the storage and loss table of the direct harmonic solve. The Newton driver takes a point context (nonlinear::solve_from_at); the nonlinear transient step passes its time, with no new history store and no second loop. The material is refused by the static load-factor driver (no time) and by every linear path, naming mat_visco::FOLLOW_UP. Two check set-ups were corrected by amendment 1, and their records were kept. Case-file key not added (recommended: viscoelastic = { base, terms, shift }, nonlinear transient study only). Follow-ups below. Follow-ups F-576, F-577. The quasi-static time-stepping driver proposed by ADR 0485 exists as nonlinear::solve_in_time (ADR 0489, 2026-11-14), with constant loads; it reproduces the loop of solve_from_at bit for bit for the viscoelastic element. Load histories and a temperature remain for its follow-up.
