C3 of ADR 0245 on each path: consistent correctors 4.7e-13 between dt 0.04 and 0.01 (3.75e-4 without C), translating cavity through step_ale_with_walls 2.2e-13 (3.06e-4 without), buoyant cavity at Ra 1e3 2.1e-14 relative between dt 0.004 and 0.001 (6.0e-5 without), 4.0e-14 with the consistent correctors too; a hydrostatic column stays at rest to 2.1e-14 and reaches rest from zero pressure to 1.6e-12 (limit 1e-10). Why not on the other paths: the fractional step's own steady cavity differs by 8.7e-2 between the two steps (a first-order defect dt R(p) without a carry-over, not C's term); coupled faces bit-inert (P1), seam floor of ADR 0076 unchanged. Case key: the optional table [solver.rhie_chow] step_consistent (default false; absent from every case's text and hash), located errors with steady, compressible, variable-density and VOF runs, the fractional step and lumped components; acts on the tree's dynamic mesh. Eight mutations caught. Follow-up proposed for the fractional step (ADR 0352 Q2).
- [~] **F-444** Co-simulation participants from the case, hosted by rcfd serve
  - depends on: F-360
  - acceptance: A case key names a moving wall patch as a co-simulation fluid participant and rcfd serve hosts it under protocol rcfd-cosim/1; a structural participant in its own process (the mock of ADR 0345) and the coupler of rcfd_fv::cosim drive it over TCP and reproduce ADR 0256 A1 and A2 with the displacements of the in-process run to 1e-12; describe of a structure may carry its elements so that the map builders of ADR 0263 run on the side of the coupler; service::Client writes a request with one call; without the key every case hash is unchanged and the schema, CLI help and MCP goldens change only by the approved additions.
  - gap: The schema gains the optional property cosim and the serve help gains [--cosim <case>]; both await the maintainer's approval (ADR 0380 Q1). Not delivered: a structure from a case, the participant's own name, more than one participant per serve, models other than incompressible flow. ADR 0380 questions Q1 to Q4 are open.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0380, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment before any run). An optional case table [cosim] (patch, participant, fixed_patches, smoothing_method, smoothing_exponent, smoothing_tolerance, initial_displacement) names a moving wall patch of an incompressible piso/pimple case as the co-simulation fluid participant (rcfd_api::cosim_case::fluid_from_case: the case's mesh is the reference, the flow starts at rest on it moved by initial_displacement, every advance smooths the interior and makes one flow step; any other model the simulation would advance is refused by name; rcfd run refuses the case), and rcfd serve --cosim <case> hosts it under rcfd-cosim/1 (cosim_case::host). On the model problem of ADR 0256 written as a case, with the mock structure of ADR 0345 in a third process and the unchanged coupled_step driving both over TCP: all 650 steps converged (7 to 10 iterations, mean 8.766, last test 9.995e-9), omega_m/omega 0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every node at every step equal to the in-process run of the same case bit for bit (limit 1e-12 X; the case also equals the hand-built CWs bit for bit over 100 steps); a structure stiffer by 1e-9 is seen (4.15e-9 X). Structure::elements (a provided method, empty by default) is carried by cosim.describe only when not empty and returned by RemoteStructure::elements, so InterfaceMap::build runs on the coupler's side with the bits of the in-process build. service::Client writes each request with one call (unit-tested; 0.047 ms per call). Without the table every case hash, written case text and baseline hash is unchanged and the MCP goldens pass unedited; the schema gains the optional property cosim and the help of serve gains [--cosim <case>], both awaiting the maintainer's approval (ADR 0380 Q1). Seven of eight mutations caught; treating fixed_patches as sliding is not seen by this model problem (its wall moves along x only, so a sliding and a fixed xmax give the same mesh; Q3). Not delivered: a structure from a case, the participant's own name (always fluid, Q2), more than one participant per rcfd serve, models other than the incompressible flow. Open: ADR 0380 Q1 to Q4. ADR 0381 (2026-11-13, F-481): MU5 is now caught by a tangential wall displacement; F-444 stays partial for the schema and serve help approval (ADR 0380 Q1). - [~] **F-445** Overset: prescribed flux on the faces between calculated and fringe cells
  - depends on: F-349, F-344
  - acceptance: An opt-in of the overset step under which the flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is the face interpolation of the interpolated fringe velocity plus one correction per closed fringe ring that makes the net flux of each enclosed part zero (ADR 0340, the switch described there): on RE of ADR 0340 at levels 1 to 3 the following coefficient a_c at both fringes is at least 0.9 at t = 0.025 and the order of R_b at t = 0.5 is at least 1.7 on both pairs, on RL the order of R_b is at least 1.7 within the parity families (levels 1 to 3 and 2 to 4), continuity of the calculated cells and the mass of the domain hold to 1e-9, the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219 holds, and without the opt-in every overset result is bit-identical; or the ADR shows with a number why the prescribed flux is not admissible.
  - gap: Coefficient a_c at t = 0.025 misses 0.9 at levels 1 and 2 (0.598 and 0.856 at the background fringe). The velocity error against the exact solution is 1.77, 1.64, 1.62 times the default's (limit 1.5). The switch as ADR 0340 words it is not admissible, and only the own-gradient variant is stable. Not a default candidate.
  - note: From ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0347, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. Built as an opt-in of the overset solver, OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux, default off, every result without it bit-identical (state hashes of two runs equal to those of the library before, baseline_hashes and the twelve existing overset test files pass unedited). The flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is the face interpolation of the velocity each pressure corrector starts from plus one correction per region of calculated cells that makes its net flux zero (it replaces the offset of the background fringe pressures). The switch as ADR 0340 words it (variant P, the interpolated fringe pressure left in the Green-Gauss gradient of the calculated cells next to the fringe) is not admissible: the Taylor-Green run on RE blows up at step 5 (level 1) and step 3 (level 2), the error growing 11-fold and 60-fold per step, as predicted before the run from the pressure mismatch of the two parts (growth with the refinement). With that gradient taken from the own part (variant G, FringeFlux::PrescribedOwnGradient) it is stable: continuity 4.5e-13, flux through the hole ring 1.9e-14, U1 3.6e-15, a uniformly accelerating flow exact to 2e-15, the flux of a ring face equal to the mean of the two cell velocities to 4e-4. Order of R_b at t = 0.5 on RE 1.962, 1.789 (default coupling 0.983, 1.015); on RL within the parity families 2.704 (levels 1 to 3) and 2.124 (2 to 4); the response per unit of truncation is 1.51, 1.54, 1.65 at levels 1 to 3 (default 0.168, 0.339, 0.497). Missed: a_c at t = 0.025 is 0.598, 0.856, 0.931 at the background fringe and 0.867, 1.037, 1.053 at the component fringe against 0.9 (levels 1 and 2 miss); diagnosed as the decay of the answer of the calculated cells over one cell (the dipole estimate made before the run gave 0.65 at level 1), not a softness of the imposition; it rises to 0.906, 0.968, 0.989 by t = 0.5. Found on the way, registered checks missed and kept as known misses: under G the interpolation error reaches the calculated cells in full, so the velocity error against the exact solution on RE is 1.77, 1.64, 1.62 times that of the default coupling (limit 1.5) and R_b itself is 9.0, 4.6, 3.3 times the default's; with the quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on both fringes the error of G falls to 0.63, 0.60, 0.56 of that and is 1.145, 1.056, 1.035 times the default's (hypothesis confirmed by its registered numbers). Not a candidate for a default. One unit check missed by round-off of its own test values (2.0e-12 against 1e-12) and was corrected by an amendment before the corrected run. Seven mutations caught. Not covered: accuracy with a moving component, RL at level 5, the combination with the other overset opt-ins beyond a smoke check. ADR 0376 (F-450), 2026-11-12: G runs with the moving, turning component of ADR 0219 without a fault (TG_1 and TG_2, quadratic stencils, continuity 6e-13, no refusal); the motion does not add to its excess over the default coupling, which sits in the calculated background cells next to the background fringe (the one-sided gradient of D5).

Bulk data is fast enough and exact by both routes: R1 (the opt-in `data.*` methods, `rcfd-data/1`, service protocol 1.2, raw `f32` on a second TCP connection) loads a 1e6-cell scalar to a GPU buffer in p50 25.9 ms, p99 57.7 ms; R2 (a reader of `store.rts` in Node) in p50 14.2 ms, p99 22.4 ms; JSON (R0) takes 552 ms. Scrubbing 30.8 and 60.1 snapshots per s at 1e6 cells, 10.5 and 17.8 at 4e6; first picture of the 1e6 surface 1.15 s (R1, first opening 1.58 s) and 0.06 s (R2); 1e6 triangles at 332 frames per s without a rate limit and p99 16.9 ms per frame with vertical sync; cold start median 0.38 s (one start of ten took 6.7 s); renderer memory 112 MB with 20 snapshots; 0 differing bits in 672e6 values; service round trip p50 0.06 ms; event latency p99 under 2.1 ms. Missed: P3, `monitors.get` of 4 series of 1e5 samples takes 127 ms against 100 ms (a 12 MB reply, most of the time on the service's side). R3 (WebAssembly) not run: it needs `unsafe` exports or `wasm-bindgen`. The rcfd-studio control, offscreen: 12.7 ms per snapshot, 73 per s, first picture 1.25 s. The registered rule has no outcome for a miss of P3 alone, so viability is the maintainer's decision; questions QA1 to QA5 of addendum 1. P3 is met after F-456 (ADR 0353, 2026-11-12): median 82.6 ms against 100; viability remains the maintainer's decision. Status check (2026-11-18, by Claude from the text of ADR 0350; no test was run again): stays PARTIAL for a reason of substance: Acceptance clauses unmet: R3 WebAssembly reader not run, P3 missed in the registered run, and the section 4 viability decision is not stated (maintainer's call, QA1 to QA5).

  - depends on: F-445, F-336
  - acceptance: With OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) and the quadratic donor interpolation of F-336, the Taylor-Green set-up of ADR 0219 with the moving, turning component (levels 1 and 2, the corrected time step of its amendment 2) is run against the default coupling with the same stencils: the largest velocity error over the calculated and fringe cells is at most 1.2 times that of the default coupling at both levels, continuity and the outflow balance hold to 1e-9 in every step, and no step is refused for a calculated cell between fringe cells on opposite sides; or the ADR names with a number what the moving fringe adds (the lag of the prescribed flux on the faces that change kind is the first candidate).

  - note: From ADR 0347 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0376, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. No library change: OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) runs with the moving, turning component as it stands. On TG_L of ADR 0219 with the quadratic donor interpolation on both runs and dt proportional to h^2 (200 and 800 steps), every step is taken (no refusal of a cell between fringe cells, no unconverged solve, no fallback), continuity 1.6e-13 and 6.2e-13, the flux into the hole region 3.8e-15 and 8.9e-15 and through the domain boundary 0, 142 and 503 kind changes. The largest error over the calculated and fringe cells is 1.2636 times that of the default coupling at level 1 (9.7081e-4 against 7.6831e-4; limit 1.2, missed, kept as a known miss) and 1.0001 at level 2 (both in the domain-boundary cell); the order of the error of G is 2.33. What the moving fringe adds, measured against the same runs with the component at rest: nothing; the excess of G over the default on the overlap is 1.21 and 1.06 moving against 1.43 and 1.10 at rest (m_G / m_default 0.844, 0.965), so the lag on the faces that change kind does not show. The excess is local to the calculated background cells within two cells of the background fringe (1.93 and 1.52 times the default there; elsewhere equal within 4 percent; the hypothesis as registered after the first run is ruled out by its deciding numbers, its maximum leaving the band at level 2), the one-sided pressure gradient of the ring cells of ADR 0347 D5. The root mean square error of each class is that of the default within 1.1 percent or smaller. Defaults untouched (two hashes equal to the library before, baseline_hashes and the existing overset tests pass). Four mutations: three caught by their checks, the fourth (the flux taken relative to the moving faces) seen only by the number of the check that already misses (1.59e4). Open: whether the alternative clause of the acceptance makes it done (ADR 0376 Q1). ADR 0409 (F-479), 2026-11-13: with the second-order ring gradient opt-in, the excess of G in the background band falls from 1.93 and 1.52 to 0.89 and 1.02 times the default coupling, and e_max(G) / e_max(default) at level 1 from 1.2636 to 1.0000. - [x] **F-452** Wave solver driven by a sampled CFD surface
  - depends on: F-333
  - acceptance: A driven boundary built from an rcfd-surface-series file reproduces, in a duct, the modal amplitudes of a closed-form duct field sampled into that file within 1 percent; a series that does not cover a whole number of periods is refused.
  - note: From ADR 0351 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE, ADR 0372, 2026-11-12. Library only. Built: rcfd-post `wave_drive.rs` (`SurfaceDrive`, `DuctFrame`, `DriveOptions`): an rcfd-surface-series section is read as a whole number of periods of a given fundamental, each harmonic of every face taken by a DFT on the file's clock (the mean dropped and reported), fitted on a hard-walled duct-mode basis, and played back periodically as the `WaveBc::Driven` ghost state of the wave entering the duct, each mode with its own axial wavenumber and impedance kz p/(rho0 omega), carried from the sampling plane to the driven faces. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a 0.12 m channel, a closed-form field of the plane wave at 1181 Hz and the plane wave and mode 1 at 2361 Hz plus a 3 Pa mean, sampled on a wall-clustered 24-face section 0.02 m upstream of the wave mesh into the file through JSON text; on 64 cells across the amplitudes measured at the inlet agree with the closed form within 8.8e-4, 3.5e-3 and 2.3e-3 (limit 1e-2; 1.4e-2 at worst on 32 across, second order: the error is the scheme's driven face, the file chain adds 1.1e-14 against a run driven by the closed form); the drive's state equals the closed form within 1.7e-13; a 128-sample two-period file is accepted and 127 and 96 samples are refused as not a whole number of periods; eleven other refusals located. Six mutations caught (plane-wave impedance, lost file clock, period test removed, wrong axial carry, harmonics played at the fundamental, Nyquist test removed). Limits: the sampled pressure must be the entering wave only; periodic signals; static section, medium at rest; only the two-dimensional channel was run; no case key or CLI (F-451). The returning-wave limit is lifted for two or more sampled sections by F-478 (ADR 0378, 2026-11-12); since then the off-plane refusal names the farthest face.

The acceptance clauses are met; two registered checks missed and one registered mutation escaped its registered check, so the item is partial by Rule I. Built: rcfd-mesh `circular_duct_ogrid` (an O-grid of a circular duct: an n x n core and four n x n/2 ring blocks, extruded along z; patches wall, inlet, outlet), and tests that drive the duct through the F-333 `AcousticWaveSolver` and measure it with `duct_modes`. The Bessel zeros are computed in the test from the power series and agree with the library within 1.1e-14. Coarse covering runs met their limits, and the rigid end without a layer reflects 0.9995. Missed: the counter-rotating (-1, 0) content of the spinning runs is 1.2e-5 against a registered 1e-6 (estimate "round-off"). Diagnosed (amendment 1): the solver commutes with the grid's rotation to 1e-15, and the content falls in a longer run, so it is left over from the start-up ramp of the drive. - [~] **F-454** Fractional step: a step-consistent face flux for the projection
  - depends on: F-443
  - acceptance: The steady lid-driven cavity of ADR 0245 C3 with solver.time_advance = "fractional_step" (8.7e-2 between dt = 0.04 and 0.01, ADR 0352 F0) is traced to its face term with a number, and either made the same to 1e-9 for the two step sizes by an opt-in (defaults bit-identical) or the ADR names why not with a number.
  - gap: The note says every acceptance clause is met. Mutation MF5 is equivalent by construction and cannot be caught. Making the opt-in the default (Q3) and done are the maintainer's call. The Chorin form is not changed, and no case key exists.
  - note: From ADR 0352 question 2, recommendation (a). ADR 0356, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL by the rule (every acceptance clause met; mutation MF5 equivalent by construction, not caught). The fractional step's 8.69e-2 between dt 0.04 and 0.01 is its face term: in a steady state the increment vanishes, the cell equations carry no step, and the face defect is dte R(p) (measured to 6.5e-16 relative), a first-order pressure smoothing. The opt-in PimpleSettings::fractional_step_consistent (incremental form; default false) takes on internal faces Gamma R(p^n) + (Gamma/dt)(c1 d^n - c2 d^{n-1}) with Gamma the harmonic face value of V/a_P of the predictor, so the steady defect is R(p)/interp(a): the steady cavity is then the same to 1.5e-13 for the two steps (1.2e-13 with the plain boundary, 1.1e-13 with BDF2, printed) and equal to the PISO step's with ADR 0245's C to 1.6e-13 (4.4e-2 without). Defaults bit for bit (fingerprints before and after equal; the rcfd-fv suites touching the changed lines and baseline_hashes unedited). The Chorin form is not changed (its cell equations carry dt; 3.7e-2 printed). No case key; outlets and periodic faces keep dte R. Four of five mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call; making the opt-in the default (Q3) is the maintainer's. With two correctors and at dt 5e-4 every Ritz value lies inside the unit circle (largest 0.970 and 0.979; most negative -0.48 and -0.78, real). With one corrector at dt 1e-3 the bounded form carries the period-two mode (at step 15 a converged pair -1.103 +- 0.346i, magnitude 1.156, and a real -1.073; the fluid part of the step a real -1.139; at step 10 a real -1.265; the magnitude matches the run's growth of about 1.15 per step), at the body (0.0025 to 0.011 from the surface, a first fluid cell at step 5), but it is not the dominant eigenvalue: pressure modes of the fluid four cells above the cylinder have eigenvalues of positive real part up to 1.93, and the first-order forcing, which runs, has them too (1.58) and a real -1.024. Partial by the registered rule: known misses E1 b to d (not real, not dominant, not at a first fluid cell at step 15), E4 (the run that runs has -1.024), and after amendment 1 S1 (those modes are not in the solid) and P3 c. Open (ADR 0392 Q2): the positive eigenvalues above one of the single corrector at dt 1e-3 in both forcings, by a linearisation of several steps along the trajectory and the channel without the cylinder. Follow-up F-494. ADR 0405 (2026-11-13, F-494): over ten steps along the trajectory the bounded form grows by 1.88 per step and the first-order forcing, which runs, by 1.31 (1.12 over twenty); the one-step eigenvalues above one belong to the early state at the body (none in the channel without the cylinder at the same Courant number, none at step 100).

With OversetSolver::set_second_order_ring_gradient(true) under PrescribedOwnGradient and the quadratic donor interpolation on both fringes, the root mean square velocity error of the calculated cells at t = 0.5 is 1.0025, 1.0007, 1.0004 times that of the default coupling with the same stencils on RE of ADR 0347 at levels 1 to 3 and 1.0013, 0.9994, 0.9994 times on RL (limit 1.05). G without the opt-in was 1.145, 1.056, 1.035 times on RE (reproduced to 3e-7), so its excess was the first-order ring gradient of D5. Continuity is at most 3.8e-13, the flux into the hole region 1.6e-14 and through the boundary 0 in every step, U1 3.6e-15 and 0, and the orders of R_b on RE are 1.964 and 1.789. An opt-in variant of the projection of F-362 evaluates the bilinear shape functions on quadrilateral structural elements (the nearest point on the bilinear patch); the default projection keeps its weights bit for bit (the F-362, F-400 and F-502 tests pass unedited). On the 3:2 walls of F-502 its weights are invariant under the eight symmetries of the square within 1e-13 and equal the test-side bilinear evaluation of ADR 0412 within 1e-13; rigid translation and rotation are reproduced and resultant, moment and work conserved within 1e-12 on a planar and on a cylindrical wall; the coupled frequency change of F-502 equals its static-compliance prediction within 10 percent for faces of 2 x 2, 4 x 4 and 8 x 8 elements.

MapMethod::BilinearProjection (MapSettings::bilinear_projection) evaluates the bilinear shape functions on quadrilateral interface elements at the nearest point of the bilinear patch (Newton from the centre with the exact Hessian, or the nearest edge point), with the projection's nearest element, offset correction and unmapped policy; on a warped patch the closed-form feet are found within 1.1e-16. The default projection and the radial basis are bit for bit unchanged (digests of rows and reports equal on the parent and the branch; the F-362, F-400, F-502 tests and the baseline hashes pass unedited). On the 3:2 walls of F-502 its weights keep all eight symmetries of the square within 9.9e-16 and equal the test-side bilinear evaluation within 6.3e-16; rigid motion within 9.3e-16 and resultant, moment and work within 1.1e-16 on the planar and cylindrical walls of F-362; the coupled frequency changes -2.17e-3, -8.18e-4, -2.82e-4 for 2 x 2, 4 x 4, 8 x 8 faces equal the static-compliance prediction within 6.6e-4 of themselves (limit 10 percent). Six mutations caught. Open: ADR 0414 Q1 (case-file exposure, needs the schema golden), Q2.
- [~] **F-505** Whirl modes above the loss of stiffness: gyroscopic stabilisation
  - depends on: F-499
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At a speed where K_eff is not positive definite the whirl problem is solved by a non-symmetric eigensolver of the state matrix written from first principles; each speed is flagged stable (all frequencies real within a registered tolerance) or unstable with the growth rate; the point mass on isotropic springs gives Omega - omega_0 and Omega + omega_0 above omega_0 within 1e-8 and is flagged stable; an anisotropic spring pair gives the closed-form unstable band between the two spring frequencies.
  - gap: No measured clause is missing. The registered odd-index check on the cube rested on a wrong torsion estimate and was met on a corrected set-up after the run (amendment 1), and one planned mutation (sign of G) is equivalent by the symmetry of the spectrum. The maintainer decides done.
  - note: From ADR 0411 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0416, 2026-11-13: whirl modes at any speed by the state matrix A = [[0, c I], [-K^/c, -G^]] of the mass-scaled gyroscopic problem, eigenvalues by Householder reduction to Hessenberg form and the Francis double-shift QR algorithm, mode vectors by inverse iteration on Q(s) = s^2 M + s G + K_eff; each speed flagged stable when max|Re s| <= 1e-8 max|s|, otherwise unstable with the growth rate max Re s (RotatingPart::whirl_state, whirl_stability with CSV, gyroscopic_state_eigen_dense); whirl_modes still reports such speeds as a loss. Isotropic point mass above omega_0: Omega - omega_0 and Omega + omega_0 within 3.3e-15 relative, both backward, flagged stable; cube on springs gyroscopically stabilised (two negative eigenvalues of K_eff, pair within 1.9e-12); anisotropic pair unstable exactly between the spring frequencies with the closed-form growth within 1.1e-14 of omega_0, band edges by bisection within 2.2e-15, the same band on the cube within 2.4e-12. Partial by the rule: the registered odd-index check on the cube rested on a wrong torsion estimate (the pre-stress cancels the spin softening on a rigid rotation about the axis; amendment 1, met on a corrected set-up after the run), and one planned mutation (sign of G in the state matrix) is equivalent by the symmetry of the spectrum. Status check (2026-11-18, by Claude from the text of ADR 0416; no test was run again): stays PARTIAL for a reason of substance: F2 and F3 (odd-index cube check) missed in run 1 and were replaced by new checks F2b/F3b on a different model after the run; mutation 2 uncaught by any registered check; ADR recommends staying partial.

Follow-up F-550 (a scale that does not vanish). - [~] **F-538** The averaged component diagonal in the relaxed PIMPLE loop
  - depends on: F-531
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The channel of ADR 0455 QF with Symmetry planes under PimpleSettings::pimple (alpha_u 0.8, alpha_p 0.5, one corrector, 10 outer iterations), whose excess over the zero-gradient planes was -0.0021 against the averaged two-corrector PISO step's 0.36, is explained by an exact linear model of the relaxed step that reproduces the measured impedance of both runs within registered limits; the dependence on alpha_u is stated.
  - gap: Open: ADR 0613 Q1 (the transient default, as ADR 0455 Q1). The registered model omitted c_x and missed C1 by 1.07e-2 (limit 5e-3) and the Symmetry parts of C3, C4, C6; the limits were met only after amendment 1, and the N 50 case is recorded as a known miss.
  - note: Numerics. PARTIAL (ADR 0613, 2026-11-15; registered before the code, amendment 1 after the registered runs). Test-only, no library line changed. The near-zero Symmetry excess of ADR 0455's relaxed PIMPLE run (pimple(nu, 10): alpha_u 0.8, alpha_p 0.5, one corrector; -0.0021 against the PISO step's 0.36) is an accidental cancellation, not a removal: at the fixed point of the relaxed outer iterations the averaged corrector turns the predictor into D + O + L/alpha_u + O D^-1 L (a sink lambda/alpha_u and an anti-sink through the neighbour links), and the unrelaxed final one-corrector iteration shifts the pressure gradient back, leaving sigma = r - (1/alpha_u - 1)(1/r - 1) of the infinite-corrector sink, r = (1/dt + 12 nu/h^2)/(1/dt + 2 nu/dy^2 + c_x); alpha_p drops out. Measured per-length excess (QF channel at 20 h and 40 h, 29 runs): sigma -0.64, -0.28, -0.010, +0.20, +0.37 at alpha_u 0.6 to 1.0 (N 100), zero at alpha_u 0.805 (0-D formula 0.8075); at N 50 the same alpha_u 0.8 gives sigma -0.42 (the Symmetry channel 5.4 percent below the zero-gradient one). An exact linear model of the relaxed step on the developed channel, with each flow-direction column's Laplacian diagonal c_x (it enters through the relaxation and a_P), reproduces the per-length impedance of the relaxed and the PISO runs within 7.2e-5 per part and every excess of the sweep within 8e-6; ADR 0455's printed impedances reproduced bit for bit; the opt-in corrected split removes the effect in the relaxed loop too (4e-6). Partial: the registered model omitted c_x and missed C1 by 1.07e-2 (limit 5e-3) and the Symmetry parts of C3, C4, C6 (record f538_registered_runs_relaxed_piso_sweep_and_n50_known_miss); met only after amendment 1. Five of five mutations caught (one only by the periodicity check). Open: ADR 0613 Q1 (the transient default, as ADR 0455 Q1). Maintainer (2026-11-18): held. The default change named above is not approved now; it would move existing flow results and waits until the fan path needs it. The other questions listed above are closed by the lead on their written recommendations.

  - depends on: F-536

This is derived so that on a periodic history of N steps per period the scale stays above sin(pi (w - 1)/N) of the period's largest (w = 18 for a floor of 1/2 at N = 100). None keeps ADR 0458's scale bit for bit, and Some(1) equals it. Totals are 2735, 2044 and 1983 outer iterations against ADR 0458's 3590, 2769 and 2436. OuterRecord gains first and scale. Defaults bit-identical (baseline_hashes and the touched rcfd-fv tests pass). Partial only by the registered rule: one mutation (the window with None) was equivalent as applied, and its corrected form, caught by the W1 check, was registered after the run; every acceptance clause is met. No case key (schema golden); docs/dynamic-mesh.md. Open: ADR 0617 Q1 to Q4. Follow-up F-692 (Case-file keys for the outer-iteration criterion and its window). Maintainer (2026-11-18): the open questions above that were listed before the standing instruction of 2026-11-11 are closed by the lead on their written recommendations, except any that would change a default result, a golden or a hash table or that needs a source; those stay as they are.

  - depends on: F-427
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Find why the one-layer ring-on-shaft fit of ADR 0507 has node pressures of 0.9955 and 1.0045 of the mean at the bottom and top, then re-register I3. Fan relevance: hub-shaft press-fit stresses.

The 8 linear cells through b - a miss Lame's constant strain sum near the bore (1.41 of it at the bore node, O(h)), so the plane-stress thickness change varies (-9.13e-6 against -7.5e-6 at the bore); its gradient, with the bottom held, tilts the bore and loads its top harder. Without Poisson or in plane strain the pressures are uniform to 1e-11 and the shaft to 1e-12. The top/bottom split falls with the radial cell (8.9e-3, 3.8e-3, 1.4e-3 at 8, 16, 32 cells), is linear in d, nearly vanishes with u_z free (1.9e-4) and grows with layers through the thickness. The reference of ADR 0507's I3 was also wrong: the shaft carries mean (1 - d/a) cos(Delta/2) = 0.9978 of the mean node pressure. I3 re-registered: in plane strain the shaft is uniform within 1e-6 (1.05e-12), the pressure is within 3.6e-3 of E d (b^2 - a^2)/(2 a b^2 (1 - nu^2)) and the hoop stress within 3.7e-3; ADR 0507's plane-stress set-up with the corrected reference is within 1e-2 (5.4e-3). The original I3 stays an ignored record. Three of three required mutations caught. No library change, no case-file key. Follow-up F-604.

Model: a frictionless hub of length L on a shaft that runs 2a past each face, same material, b = 2a, d = 1e-3 a, an eighth of the fit in Hex8 with 6-degree sectors. The shaft's node planes are offset by 0.05 of a cell, so every bore node lies inside one shaft face. At mid-length the pressure matches the free-ended (sigma_zz = 0) closed form E d (b^2 - a^2)/(2 a b^2), within 2.1e-3 at L = 4 (b - a) and 3.4e-3 at L = 8 (b - a), and not the plane-strain one. With u_z = 0 everywhere the plane-strain value comes back within 7.6e-3. The edge pressure peak is at the hub faces on every mesh and diverges as the Williams exponent 0.774 of a 90-degree corner on a half-space predicts: the face row grows by 1.124, 1.148 and 1.160 per halving, toward 1.170. The band resultants converge: the last quarter of b - a gives 1.157 p_0, with orders 1.4 to 1.6 and a last change of 4.0e-3. The fan's shaft and bore dimensions are not in the repository; as a nominal illustration, a 1.5 mm shaft needs 0.19 mm bore cells.   - note: Structural solver, advanced tier. Follow-up of F-679 (ADR 0602). PARTIAL. ADR 0606, 2026-11-15: the centrifugal pre-stress of a free cyclic sector. The cyclic constraint leaves two of a free body's six rigid motions at index 0, the axial translation and the rotation about the axis (derived in the ADR); the centrifugal load is orthogonal to both, so two linear gauge constraints at one interior node (axial and tangential translation) carry exactly no reaction and give the free stress. RotatingSector::new with stress stiffening and the opt-in RotatingOptions::free_sector_prestress (default false) now solves the free sector this way (rotating::free_sector_unit_static), and refuses a sector with supports or other constraints. On the free Beam2 ring of ADR 0602, two meshes: the pre-stress equals the constrained-copy route within 9e-15 (limit 1e-10), the residual at the interior nodes is 1.9e-14 of the load, the gauge node does not matter (3.3e-15), and the ADR 0602 whirl frequencies are unchanged within 4.0e-12 (limit 1e-10). Without the option the free sector is still refused, and the defaults are bit-identical (baseline_hashes and the existing rotating tests pass). Eight of nine mutations were caught; the one that escaped took the branch with stress stiffening off, which changes no frequency because the operator scales the geometric stiffness by zero, and the check compared frequencies only. Not covered: supported or otherwise constrained sectors with the opt-in, solid and shell sectors, and RotatingPart::new on a free part. Follow-up F-683 (The free-sector pre-stress on solid and shell sectors, and its scope without stress stiffening).

The ADR 0614 sweep (6 x 6 x 6 patch, every boundary node fixed, 51 stretches on [0.5, 1]) repeated for confined compression at nu = 0.3, 0.45, 0.49 and uniaxial stress at nu = 0.45, 0.49, against a closed-form acoustic bound for the neo-Hookean energy at diag(t, t, lambda) derived in the ADR (q = min over the polar angle of mu J^-2/3 (1 + mu_-), equal to the numerical sphere minimum to 3.8e-5): the stabilised element's lowest eigenvalue stays >= 0.977 mu in every case and lies between the plain element and the Full Hex8 at every stretch (an ordering derived in the ADR, which holds whether or not the Full Hex8 locks); the Full Hex8 stays above q everywhere. The plain element has a spurious zero in every case: lambda_s = 0.6418 (confined, nu 0.3), 0.8094 (0.45), 0.9507 (0.49: 5 per cent compression), 0.5644 and 0.5103 (uniaxial, 0.45, 0.49). Finding: near incompressibility the coefficient (up to 6507 mu) drives the stabilised element to within 0.15 to 0.6 per cent of the Full Hex8, which locks there (at rest the Full Hex8 is 13 per cent stiffer than the plain element at nu = 0.49). Not covered: tension, shear and free boundaries, other materials, a locking-free reference of the compressed state, a coefficient without the bulk modulus. Follow-up F-703 (A deviatoric coefficient for the stabilised incompatible-modes Hex8 near incompressibility). F-703 measures the stabilisation against F-bar on the same patch; near incompressibility the ADR 0614 coefficient's softest mode is 7 to 16 per cent stiffer than F-bar, and no coefficient without the bulk modulus stabilises confined compression at nu >= 0.45.

(1) On a linear fan curve dp = 100 (1 - Q/0.05) Pa against three quadratic systems that put Q at 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of 0.05 m^3/s, the per-point flows are within 1e-9 relative of the closed form and the mean, worst, weighted (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) and mean-plus-one-sigma flows are 0.025, 0.0125, 0.02125 and 0.025 - 0.0125 sqrt(2/3) m^3/s within 1e-12 relative of the same aggregation done by hand on the per-point values. (2) With blade mass errors N(0, sigma) on Z = 7 blades, the mean static unbalance is within 4 standard errors of r_c m sigma sqrt(Z pi / 4) at N = 4096 samples, and a metric linear in one Gaussian tolerance gives mean + k sd within 4 standard errors of a + k |b| sigma. (4) Objective vectors, constraint violations and ledger lines (fixed clock) are bit-identical for 1, 2, 3 and 8 workers and for two runs with the same seed, and differ for another seed. (5) On the reduced-order fan (rcfd_post::fan_rom) at three impedance points the layer's objective values equal, bit for bit, the same aggregation of FanRomEvaluator::metrics called directly, and flow falls strictly as the system coefficient rises. (6) Nelder-Mead and CMA-ES find the closed-form constrained optimum (speed scale 1.2, pitch 0.3, mean shaft power 3.6 W) within the registered limits, and the NSGA-II front lies within the registered distance of the closed-form front. (7) baseline_hashes, the existing design tests and both tools-list goldens are unchanged.

FanRomTarget evaluates the ADR 0119 reduced-order fan on a ComputerFan with flow, pressure rise, power, efficiency, tone1_pa, tone1_db, the A-weighted sum of the first three tones and the static-unbalance force of the specimen's blades. Checks: linear fan against three quadratic systems, per-point flows within 1.4e-16 of the closed form and mean, worst, weighted and mean-plus-sigma flows equal to the hand aggregation; mean static unbalance of N(0, sigma) blade mass errors on 7 blades within 1.7 SE of r_c m sigma sqrt(7 pi / 4) at 4096 samples and a linear Gaussian metric's mean + 2 sd within 1.5 SE; the violation of the one violated point is 0.75 exactly, a stalled point fails the candidate with a located reason (linear fan and reduced-order fan), feasible violation exactly 0; objective vectors, violations and ledger bytes identical for 1, 2, 3 and 8 workers and for two runs, all 32 differ for another seed; reduced-order objective values bit-equal to FanRomEvaluator::metrics aggregated by hand, flow strictly falling as the system coefficient rises; Nelder-Mead and CMA-ES reach the constrained optimum (speed scale 1.2, pitch 0.3, 3.6 W) within 4e-8 relative in power and the robust optimum of the sampled plan, NSGA-II front within 1.8 percent of the closed-form front over the full flow range; baseline_hashes, the design tests and the tools-list goldens unchanged. The proposal loop from 10 initial points reaches within 1 percent of the Branin minimum 0.397887 on at least 18 of 20 seeds within 60 evaluations with a median of at most 35, where uniform random search reaches it on at most 4 of 20; on Hartmann 6 it reaches within 1 percent of -3.32237 on at least 5 of 10 seeds within 200 evaluations and on at least 2 more seeds than CMA-ES (ADR 0222) and differential evolution at the same budget; with a region of failed evaluations it still reaches the Branin target on at least 18 of 20 seeds with at most 25 percent failed evaluations after the initial design; on the reduced-order fan model (ADR 0119) it comes within 1 percent of the best of a 21^3 factorial reference within 50 evaluations on at least 9 of 10 seeds. Checks: two-point closed form within 2.7e-15, likelihood gradient within 1e-9, leave-one-out within 2e-15 of refits, EI within 3e-14 of quadrature; coverage 0.938 on prior draws (0.865 with a wrong length scale), hyperparameters recovered (median length scale 0.174 for 0.2); the Branin minimum within 1 percent on 20 of 20 seeds in a median of 28 evaluations (random search 0 of 20), Hartmann 6 on 6 of 10 within 55 evaluations against CMA-ES 1 and DE 0 at 200, a failure disc avoided (3 percent failed against 86 percent without the failure handling), noisy Branin 20 of 20, a constraint 10 of 10; on the reduced-order fan (stagger, chord and camber scales, power at three impedance points) 10 of 10 runs within 1 percent of a 9261-point grid optimum by evaluation 22, with every failure located; ledger resume, shuffled lines, worker counts and replay bit-equal; baseline_hashes and the design and tools-list tests unchanged. (2) A scripted investigator that reads 60 exploratory points and registers the 12 best-looking claims per world, on 400 seeded synthetic worlds (12 parameters, 4 metrics, planted true, boundary and zero effects, known noise, 64 pairs per test), makes a false confirmation in at most 37 of the 400 worlds and confirms at least 95 percent of the large planted effects it registers; the levels spent in one ledger sum to at most 0.05 and the count continues across a reopened ledger; a single test at the boundary effect has a confirmation rate within 4 standard errors of its level; the registered negative controls fail as stated (a scripted agent that tests on the exploratory data without correction false-confirms in at least 300 of 400 worlds, one that stops at the first favourable look in at least 40 of 400, and the protocol with a constant level 0.05 exceeds 37). (5) A result line written by hand through the ledger append is never reported: 0 of 5 returned, 5 of 5 flagged. - [x] **F-705** Design store header after a torn first write
  - depends on: F-268

Store bytes of the existing paths unchanged (5 FNV digests measured before the fix), every existing store, study, ledger, design integration and rcfd-mcp test passes unedited, baseline hashes pass. Four of four mutations caught. Not covered: a real killed process, a power loss without fsync, two writers.

- [~] **F-712** Symmetry planes and a uniform in-plane flow on the annulus interface pair
  - depends on: none
  - acceptance: the uniform in-plane flow of ADR 0637 UT on the frozen join of annulus_3d_cylindrical_interface with zmin, zmax symmetry (2.4e-2 after one step) is diagnosed; either it is kept to 1e-10 with the cause fixed and every changed default result listed for the maintainer, or the limitation is documented with its cause.
  - gap: The cause is diagnosed, but the 1e-10 flow is kept only with the opt-in corrected component diagonal; making it the default would change baseline hashes, goldens and 11 tests, for the maintainer's decision (F-738). One test of the flipped run was not run; the lag preflight mutation is not checked.
  - note: ADR 0650, 2026-11-16: the uniform in-plane flow of ADR 0637 UT on the frozen join of annulus_3d_cylindrical_interface with zmin, zmax symmetry. Cause (diagnosed and registered before any run): the default averaged momentum diagonal of the PISO split. On the one-cell-deep pair every cell touches both planes, and their Dirichlet term on u_z makes the in-plane HbyA a fraction lambda of U, which acts as a uniform spurious drag k = 4 nu / (3 lz^2) = 13.3 s^-1. The pressure balances the drag with a linear field. The Green-Gauss cell gradient of that field is wrong in the wall cells, where the pressure is zero-gradient on the fixed-velocity walls, so the wall cells deviate by about (1 - lambda)/2. The cause is not the frozen join, the mesh or the symmetry face values: the default misses by the same amount on a conformal annulus_3d (2.34e-2, against 2.36e-2 on the join, both in an outer wall cell), the pressure slope is -k U to 5e-4, and zero-gradient planes keep the flow (1.4e-15). With the existing opt-in solver.component_diagonal = "corrected" (ADR 0010, ADR 0074 W1) the flow is kept to 7.8e-16 on the frozen join over 40 steps, 8.9e-16 on the conformal annulus and 7.9e-15 through [mesh.sliding] with coinciding nodes; the default is unchanged. Making corrected the default would move the baseline_hashes row packed_bed, the settings hashes and goldens, the last bits of 3-D transient piso/pimple results, and 11 tests in the 49 files checked (component_diagonal, w34c W1a, duct_diagnosis A6, lumped z4 twice, consistent_correctors_case_f301 c1 and c4, cosim_case_f444 k2 and k3, film_gas_f292 d3 and d3b); one test of the flipped run was not run. Three of four mutations caught; the fourth targeted the lag preflight, which no check runs. Follow-up F-738 (Corrected component diagonal as the default). Status check (2026-11-18, by Claude from the text of ADR 0650; no test was run again): stays PARTIAL for a reason of substance: Amendment 1 corrected the B2 set-up (C3 kept as ignored record), but one B3 test was not run, mutation MU2 (lag preflight) is not checked, and making corrected the default (F-738) is open.

  - depends on: F-697
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: ComputerFan::default() through RomFan::from_axial_fan runs unstalled at 3000 rpm for every flow above 40 percent of its free delivery in the reduced-order model, every ADR 0118 schema, checker and ensemble test keeps its result, and no golden or hash table changes (or the needed change is listed for the maintainer before any edit).

Why ComputerFan::default() stalls in the reduced-order model (registered, checked on the base code): at 3000 rpm its free delivery is 0.0765 m^3/s and is already loaded (free discharge needs dp_t = rho c_x^2 / 2 + swirl; 83 percent of dp_t is the exit dynamic pressure), so every strip sits at 2.1 to 6.0 deg of the 10.03 deg attached window (cl_max 1.1 / 2 pi); with its high flow coefficient (0.46 at the tip at free delivery) the tip inflow angle rises 14.4 deg down to 0.4 q_f, and the outer strips stall from 0.79 q_f. Neither from_axial_fan nor the model is at fault. A default meeting the acceptance needs a hub zero-lift angle of about 58 deg or more (lossless bound), which the ADR 0118 checker variants "axial fit" and "root off hub" do not allow together (estimate: hub stagger at most about 54 deg). Negative controls: stagger -8 deg stalls from 0.555 q_f, cl_max 0.8 from 0.451. Four of four mutations caught. No library file, golden or hash table changed. Open for the maintainer: whether a ROM-usable schema fan replaces the default (re-basing the ADR 0118 axial-fit variant, s4 and the FEM blade tests) or sits beside it (recommended). Follow-up F-722 (Reduced-order reference fan in the schema).

  - depends on: F-699
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: a registered check on a synthetic noise source on which the one-standard-error rule alone would trust a correction shows the correction untrusted only because the discrepancy is not above twice the stated uncertainty (and trusted with that guard off), the mutation stated uncertainty ignored fails it, P4 searches its messages with the file path removed, and every ADR 0622 check keeps its result.
  - note: Follow-up of F-699 (ADR 0622). ADR 0642, 2026-11-16. DONE. Test-only change, no library file edited (defaults and every ADR 0622 result keep their bits). The uncertainty guard of the fidelity driver is now isolated by a registered check on an offset-noise source S8 (high = low + 0.075 + 0.01 z, stated uncertainty 0.05): in all 4 rounds the one-standard-error rule picks R1add with a leave-one-out RMSE of 0.12 to 0.14 of the uncorrected one (limit 0.8), the discrepancy is 1.55 to 1.65 times the stated uncertainty, and the correction is untrusted only because it is not above twice that uncertainty (screening bit-identical to no correction); with the guard off (k_u 0) and with factor 1 the same fit is trusted in every round. The mutation "stated uncertainty ignored", which survived ADR 0622, fails it, as do the guard removed, the factor 2 dropped and the guard inverted. P4 now searches its messages with the table path removed and asserts the path is named, on a directory deliberately holding a cell text (the old form fails there; it stays as an ignored set-up record); it catches a malformed cell, a measured value and a missing path put into the message. All 15 remaining ADR 0622 fast tests and its heavy record pass with the same numbers (B1 0.359 and 0.115, B2 0, NC1 0.058, B4 0.063). - [~] **F-718** Gaussian-process discrepancy rung R3 for the fidelity driver
  - depends on: F-699, F-698
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: with F-698's Gaussian process on the R2 residual (zero mean, nugget from the stated uncertainty, hyperparameters fixed per fit and leave-one-out from the closed form), R3 is chosen over R2 only by the one-standard-error rule, its leave-one-out residuals equal brute force within 1e-8, its 2-sigma leave-one-out coverage is at least the registered value on a smooth nonlinear synthetic discrepancy, and every ADR 0622 check keeps its result.
  - gap: Every clause is met; the predictive standard deviation missed 1e-8 on two noise-free fits (1.6e-8 and 6.3e-8), shown later to be errors of the double-precision reference (closed form within 1.3e-10 and 8.1e-10, ADR 0656). Verified on synthetic sources only.
  - note: Follow-up of F-699 (ADR 0622, 2026-11-15). ADR 0652, 2026-11-16. PARTIAL (every acceptance clause met on the corrected runs; the leave-one-out standard deviation misses 1e-8 on the two noise-free fits). Library only, opt-in (TrustRule::r3, default None; no case key, no MCP tool): rung R3 of the fidelity driver is R2 plus a zero-mean Gaussian process (F-698's squared-exponential kernel and Cholesky factorisation) on the R2 residual, with the nugget from the high source's stated uncertainty, length scales and process variance fitted once per fit by maximum likelihood (analytic gradient, F-698's multi-start pattern) and held in every fold, and leave-one-out residuals from a closed form that includes the refit of the R2 coefficients, e3_i = ((G r)_i + e2_i (G P)_ii) / G_ii; R3 needs 10 d pairs and a residual above the rounding level, is chosen over R2 only by the one-standard-error rule (recomputed by the test in every fit), and is trusted only with 2-sigma leave-one-out coverage at least 0.8. Checks: leave-one-out residuals equal brute force (R2 refitted, the process re-solved) within 2.5e-10 to 4e-14 of the residual scale; coverage 0.95 to 1.00 against the registered 0.85 on a smooth nonlinear synthetic discrepancy with and without noise; R3 chosen on it (RMSE 0.006 and 0.27 of R2's), not chosen on unstructured noise or an exact affine source; through the driver (two parameters, 300 candidates, 36 promotions) R3 is chosen from round 4 and its held-out RMSE is 0.078 of the R2 fit's; flagged queries get the constant only, bit for bit; the correction round-trips bit for bit; no R3 number reaches the public ledger with a private source; with R3 off the S1, S4 and private S7 ledgers are byte-identical to before, and every ADR 0622 check (including the heavy fan record) keeps its result. Ten of ten mutations caught. Misses recorded: the registered design chose R3 on a rounding-level residual (fixed by a floor in amendment 1), and the predictive sd differs from brute force by 1.6e-8 and 6.3e-8 of the residual scale on noise-free fits (cancellation, limit 1e-8). Verified on synthetic sources only. Follow-up F-734 (Fidelity driver R3: the leave-one-out standard deviation through the Cholesky factor). Follow-up F-735 (A zero-mean, absolute-noise mode of F-698's Gaussian process used by R3). The L3s misses recorded by ADR 0652 (6.3e-8 and 1.6e-8 of the residual scale) are errors of its double-precision brute-force reference; against a double-double reference the closed form agreed within 1.3e-10 and 8.1e-10 (ADR 0656, 2026-11-16). R3's zero-mean process is now F-698's zero-mean mode (ADR 0663, 2026-11-16); its fits are bit-identical to before. Status check (2026-11-18, by Claude from the text of ADR 0652; no test was run again): stays PARTIAL for a reason of substance: Registered L3s (limit 1e-8) missed on two noise-free fits and is kept as a known_miss; S2 on N3 also missed in the registered design and was fixed by a library rounding floor in amendment 1.

  - depends on: none

Cause of the failed scheduled runs of 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15: cargo fmt --all hands every target root (63802 characters on the runner) to one rustfmt process, above the Windows limit of 32767 (os error 206, reproduced locally); the fmt step now runs cargo fmt -p per workspace member (largest 20031 characters), with the same set of files checked. gate.yml: cron daily 02:00 UTC on main, workflow_dispatch kept; a decide job (actions: read) skips a scheduled run when the last run whose full gate, windows-latest job passed on main tested the same SHA, and runs the gate when the query fails. After a failed test step, scripts/gate_attribute.py re-runs each failed test once (flaky when it passes), looks it up in the test-to-ADR index, and lists the first-parent commits since the last green gate that touched the test's file or crate (direct) or a dependency's sources (dependency), with their F-items and ADRs. It can bisect over those commits (input bisect, time budget bisect_minutes), and it writes gate-out/attribution.json, a job-summary table and, with input open_issues, one issue per non-flaky failure from a separate job with issues: write. scripts/adr_test_index.py finds tests statically (501 of 501 binaries and 99.0 % of the rows of a real gate listing) and maps them by file-name item, ADR and roadmap citations of the file or function, and module path: 1053 of 1134 integration-test binaries (92.9 %) and 6986 of 7472 tests (93.5 %) map to an ADR, and 20 of 20 sampled binaries have a correct ADR. Cause of the camber_seam_h fold on the reference located before the design: with the axial front edge every suction-side nose target lies on the pressure side of the extended camber line once front_gap tan(stagger) exceeds the corner offset (at every front_gap and n_nose), and the pursuit lines turn by up to the stagger after the stack. New opt-in construction S beside it, CGridOptions::camber_seam_s_construction() = camber_seam_h + camber_front (front edge front_gap chords along the extended leading-edge camber line, centre line straight to it and turning axial upstream) + straight_lines (straight segments from the stack edge to the targets, first cell stretched by 1/cos) + no radial filter (amendment 1: the filter folds the first free rows at the mid-span kink of the station distribution); no case value. - [x] **F-727** Hypothesis record, seeded re-run sample and evidence-parameter guard
  - depends on: F-701
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: verify with a registered sample of k evidence pairs (derived seed, k recorded in the result) catches an impostor evaluator on at least the registered share of synthetic worlds; a check that edits one evidence parameter and rewrites the reference hashes is refused only by the parameter comparison (the mutation parameters not compared fails it); every ADR 0624 check keeps its result.
  - note: Follow-up of F-701 (ADR 0624 questions 3 and 5). ADR 0662, 2026-11-16. DONE. Library only, opt-in: a hypothesis registration may carry a seeded re-run sample (design::hypothesis RerunSample: k pairs, rtol, atol), drawn by a partial Fisher-Yates from a seed derived from the record hash and seed (rerun_seed, rerun_pairs); verify re-runs both arms of exactly the sampled pairs with the trusted evaluator at analytic, reduced-order or cfd tier (measured refused) and the result line records k, the seed and the pairs. rerun_sample_size gives the smallest k from the hypergeometric miss probability C(n-b,k)/C(n,k); for 64 pairs and an evaluator wrong on 16 of them, k = 13 (miss 0.0147). Checks: on 400 synthetic worlds an impostor wrong on the high arm of 16 of 64 pairs is caught in 394 (limit 380, the registered share 0.95), the number of re-run problems equals the sampled corrupted pairs in 400 of 400, the honest evaluator is never flagged, without a sample at tier cfd it is caught in 0 and with k = 1 in 116 (66 to 134); editing one evidence parameter (a domain value, a factor level, a compensating parameter) and rewriting the result's parent hash leaves exactly one problem, the parameter comparison, in 3 of 3, and the mutation that removes the comparison (ADR 0624's M15, which survived there) now fails. Records without a sample keep their bytes (a ledger of main's code reproduced byte for byte, the G1 hash unchanged) and are read as before; ADR 0624 code reading a new record ignores the sample. Every ADR 0624 check keeps its numbers (S1 1, S2 1592 of 1595, NC1 400, NC2 61, NC3 75, S4 118). Nine mutations caught. Not covered: the sample is derivable from the file, so it guards against mistakes and version drift, not a deliberate forger; no MCP tool (F-702). Follow-up F-745 (Verifier-drawn re-run sample for hypotheses from evaluators outside the maintainer's control). ADR 0693 (F-745, 2026-11-17): a verifier-drawn sample from a seed outside the file (verify_drawn) catches an evaluator that is honest exactly on the F-727 sample, which that sample never catches.
- [x] **F-728** Coupled held metrics and the held-tolerance resolution floor for hypotheses
  - depends on: F-701
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: two held metrics (flow and speed) solved together on a synthetic evaluator with a known joint solution within the registered tolerance, the floor from the held tolerance computed against a closed form, a registration below that floor refused with both values named, and every ADR 0624 check keeps its result.
  - note: Follow-up of F-701 (ADR 0624 question 4). ADR 0665, 2026-11-16. DONE. Library only, opt-in: design::hypothesis register_with_floor(ledger, h, model) registers a hypothesis with one or two held metrics; two are solved together in each arm by a damped, projected Newton iteration on the held residuals (forward-difference Jacobian, backtracking on the tolerance-scaled residual, inside the brackets; Dennis and Schnabel 1983, cited from memory), and the registration computes the held-tolerance floor (held_floor): at the domain midpoint, phi = sum_j |S_j| tol_j per solved arm with S = J^-T grad y by differences, summed over both arms for value targets and the high arm for as_low_arm targets, the first-order change of a paired difference that the tolerances allow; a min_effect below 10 times it is refused with both values named. The floor is stored in the registration entry (settings.held_floor), verify requires it for two holds and recomputes it with the evaluator. Checks on a synthetic flow-and-speed evaluator with closed forms (q = b n A, n = a B / (G (1 + 0.2 b)), power = a b C): 64 of 64 arms within the tolerances (1e-6, 1e-5) in 10 evaluations each, every solved parameter within twice its first-order bound of the closed-form joint solution, the mean change 0.0243761 within 8.7e-9 of the closed form (limit the floor 2.04e-6), confirmed; the floor within 2.8e-11 relative of the closed form (single hold 1.9e-13, as_low_arm 2.9e-13); min_effect 2e-5 below 10 x 2.04e-6 refused naming both, 2.1e-5 accepted; a decoupled sweep leaves q off by 0.088 and 0.30, holding the flow alone moves the answer by 6.5e-4 (negative controls); the floor removed, too large or edited, a second compensating parameter or held metric edited are each caught; void, resume and worker-count bytes as in ADR 0624. register and register_batch keep one hold and their bytes (single-hold ledgers byte-identical to the base); every ADR 0624 check keeps its numbers (S1 1, S2 1592 of 1595, NC1 400, NC2 61, S4 118) and every ADR 0662 one (A1 394, NC7 116). Ten of ten mutations caught (the backtracking one recorded, it survives). Not covered: three or more holds, mixed targets, batches with two holds, the floor away from the domain midpoint; no MCP tool (F-702). Follow-up F-749 (Held-tolerance floor over a sample of the design). ADR 0670 (F-749, 2026-11-16): the held-tolerance floor may be taken over a registered seeded sample of the design (floor_sample); midpoint registrations keep their bytes and every ADR 0665 check keeps its numbers.

  - depends on: F-707

  - note: Moving immersed shapes at lock-in, a transversely oscillating cylinder shedding vortices. Follow-up of F-707 (ADR 0648). Re 100, A/D 0.5, f D/U 0.14, in the square of half side 8 D with a Freestream far field, PISO with linear upwind, dt = T/700 for every run, 20 periods, window the last 4; immersed on a Cartesian D/40 core against the body-fitted swept-volume ALE run on a 256 x 128 O-grid mapped to the same square, started on the grid at the initial pose (fast test T5, which catches the F-707 survivor). Met: mean drag 0.8220 against 0.8189 (0.37 per cent, limit 4.0), lift phase -96.4 against -103.3 degrees (6.9, limit 8.0), phase change across the bracket 5.9 degrees (limit 25), mean lift, the 128 x 64 reference within its limits; with the body velocity left out of the forcing the lift is 21 times larger and 131 degrees off. Missed (limits unchanged, known-miss record): lift amplitude 0.0551 against 0.0478 (15 per cent, limit 8.3) and complex harmonic 20 per cent (limit 12.3), because the first lift harmonic nearly cancels at this point (0.048 against 0.178 for the fixed cylinder; it changes by 43 per cent across the bracket, limit 25), absolute differences 0.007 to 0.010; the immersed lift's harmonics above the fifth hold 13 per cent of its rms (staircase cell crossings, limit 5); the negative control's mean drag differs by only 2.2 per cent (limit: more than 4.0). Not included: other amplitudes and frequencies, a map of the lock-in range and the phase jump, a case-file key (open, F-307 schema golden), rotating or deforming shapes, BDF2, three dimensions. - [~] **F-732** The inverted iterate of the incompatible-modes Hex8 at the punch edge of a distorted mesh (ADR 0649 DB4)
  - depends on: F-719
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The punch block of ADR 0649 on the 8^3 mesh at 0.25 h (seed 0xF719_0008) with rule L: the cause of the inverted point at 67.5 per cent of the load located (the incompatible-mode field of the element against the compatible one along the path); the driver's line search, and an opt-in backtracking of the mode update when a point inverts, each measured on the same set-up; if one passes the load, reaction and displacement within the ADR 0636 tolerance (10 per cent) of the F-bar Hex8 and the loaded state positive definite; the plain element on the 4^3 mesh at 0.25 h reported; the default bits unchanged.
  - gap: Only one of five mutations of the backtracking was caught by registered checks. The line search alone fails and the backtracking alone fails at 0.89; only both together pass. Not covered: a sufficient-decrease test, other meshes and seeds, other materials (F-739).
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier. Follow-up of F-719 (ADR 0649 DB4). PARTIAL. ADR 0655, 2026-11-16: the inverted point of the stabilised incompatible-modes Hex8 (rule L) at the punch edge of the 8^3 block at 0.25 h (seed 0xF719_0008). Cause located: not the compatible field and not the converged enhanced field (both keep det F >= 0.88 along the path at element 476), but a Newton iterate of the element's local mode iteration from alpha = 0 overshooting into det F < 0 (the second iterate at -1.31 at the failing load), within a band of the path entered at 67.5 per cent of the load. New opt-in SolidModel::set_incompatible_mode_backtracking (default off; an inverted mode iterate halves its step, at most 20 times): no default bit changed (the bit records of ADR 0506, 0608, 0614, 0630 and the rcfd-api baseline hashes pass; with the opt-in, bitwise identical results on two set-ups that do not need it). Measured on the same set-up: the driver's line search alone fails as the default (0.675); the backtracking alone passes 0.675 but fails at 0.89 (element 475, the damped mode iteration not converged in 25 steps); the two together pass: punch reaction and corner displacement within 7.5 and 2.9 per cent of the F-bar Hex8, loaded state positive definite (reported, not a registered pass). The plain element on the 4^3 block at 0.25 h passes with the backtracking alone (6.9 and 3.8 per cent of F-bar), the same cause. One of five mutations of the backtracking caught by the registered checks (the others only change reported rows). Not covered: a sufficient-decrease test in the backtracking, the combination on other meshes and seeds, other materials. Follow-up F-739 (The line search with the backtracking of the incompatible-mode update as a registered remedy on distorted meshes (ADR 0655 question 1)). ADR 0658 (F-739, 2026-11-16): the combination reported by ADR 0655 is registered and checked in F-739: it passes the eight distorted meshes of ADR 0649 (DB4 at 7.5 and 2.9 per cent, positive definite) and one of three further seeds of the 8^3 block at 0.25 h; the mutations of the backtracking that escaped ADR 0655 are all caught there.
- [~] **F-733** Basin restart on a second multimodal function and on the fan
  - depends on: F-715
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: on Shekel 10 or a registered second multimodal function, and on the F-698 R1 fan set-up, the restart of ADR 0651 with its registered tau and rho reaches the target on at least as many seeds as plain expected improvement, a check decides whether the fresh process of the restart is needed (the surviving mutation R2), and a hash of the default proposal points of the F-698 O1 run pins the default bits.

  - note: Follow-up of F-715 (ADR 0651, 2026-11-16). ADR 0673, 2026-11-17. PARTIAL (library, opt-in). The basin restart of ADR 0651 with its registered tau 1e-4 and rho 2 was run on a second multimodal function and on the fan. On Shekel 10 (n0 10, budget 150, seeds 1 to 20) it reached the minimum within 1 percent on 17 of 20 seeds against 18 of 20 for plain expected improvement: registered limit missed, kept as a known-miss record. On the seeds it misses (two of them solved by plain expected improvement), the restart fires at evaluations 44 to 53 from a local basin and its 91 to 103 picks never come near the narrow global basin that plain expected improvement still finds later, so a small acquisition does not mean plain expected improvement is stuck. On the F-698 R1 fan set-up (seeds 1 to 10, 50 evaluations) every run is bit-equal to plain expected improvement (10 of 10 within 1 percent of the grid optimum, F-698 failed counts reproduced exactly): the restart never fires, because the fitted length scales (2 to 10 in the unit cube) put the whole box inside the basin. BayesOptions::restart gains Restart::step_model (default false), which scores the restart by the step's own process; on Shekel 10 it does 11 of 20 against 17 for the fresh process, so the fresh process is needed and the surviving F-715 mutation R2 is now caught. Shekel 10 minimum (from memory) confirmed numerically at -10.536443. Six of six mutations caught; a fast check that made no restart pick within 40 evaluations was corrected under a recorded amendment. Not covered: a trigger that detects repetition rather than a small acquisition, a multimodal fan objective, tau and rho beyond Hartmann 6. Follow-up F-758 (A repetition trigger for the basin restart).
- [~] **F-734** Fidelity driver R3: the leave-one-out standard deviation through the Cholesky factor
  - depends on: F-718
  - milestones: fan
  - acceptance: the predictive standard deviation of R3 is evaluated without the cancellation of a^T C a, it equals brute force within 1e-8 of the residual scale on the noise-free fits of ADR 0652 (N1a and the driver's final fit), and every ADR 0652 and ADR 0622 check keeps its result.
  - gap: Every acceptance clause is met; one registered mutation (restoring the old a^T C a) survived because that form also agrees within 8.1e-10. Verified on synthetic fits only (n up to 40, two parameters).
  - note: Follow-up of F-718 (ADR 0652, 2026-11-16). ADR 0656, 2026-11-16. PARTIAL (every acceptance clause met; one registered mutation survived because the replaced form proved accurate too). Library only, opt-in (behind TrustRule::r3, default None): R3's leave-one-out predictive standard deviation is now evaluated as the conditional variance 1/G_ii = 1/|L^-1 e_i|^2 plus the variance of the R2 refit |L^T q_i|^2 through the Cholesky factor (q_i from the deletion formula of least squares), both sums of squares, instead of a_i^T C a_i; the ADR derives it from first principles. Against a brute force in double-double arithmetic (about 32 digits) it agrees within 1.3e-10 (N1a) and 9.2e-10 (the driver's final fit) of the residual scale on the noise-free fits of ADR 0652 (limit 1e-8), and within 2e-15 with noise. Every ADR 0652 test and every ADR 0622 test (including the heavy fan record) passes, R3's published numbers and coverage are unchanged, and default runs never reach the changed code. Four of five mutations caught. The fifth, which restores ADR 0652's old a^T C a, also agrees with the double-double reference within 8.1e-10: the 6.3e-8 and 1.6e-8 misses of ADR 0652 came from that test's double-precision brute force (unit-vector solves at condition about 2e9), not from cancellation in the closed form. Verified on synthetic fits only (n up to 40, two parameters).

  - depends on: F-725
  - acceptance: an opt-in setting couples the two faces of every periodic pair implicitly in the momentum matrix (the partner's new value, as the pressure equation already does), with the defaults bit-identical; on ADR 0661's lockstep the sector's largest difference from the full annulus with one outer iteration is within a registered limit of ADR 0661's six-outer-iteration variant V(6, 6) (6.0e-3) on every step, and ADR 0641's step-1 difference falls below a registered limit.   - note: ADR 0664, 2026-11-16: implicit momentum coupling of periodic pairs. The opt-in PimpleSettings::rotational_periodic_implicit (default false) puts the rotated partner of every rotationally periodic pair into the momentum predictor implicitly (translational pairs are implicit since ADR 0046): the partner term coef (R u_partner)_k becomes the entries coef R_kj of one block system of the active components, its lagged value leaves the right-hand side, the components are assembled from the same iterate and solved together (BiCGStab, ILU(0)), and the correctors' H operator includes the links. On ADR 0661's lockstep (the sector SS against the full annulus, 400 steps from the start consistent with the inlet) one outer iteration with the setting stays within 2.4e-4 U_in of the six-outer-iteration variant V(6, 6) on every step (limit 1.5e-3; field form 3.3e-4), largest difference 5.89e-3 against V(6, 6)'s 5.99e-3; ADR 0641's step-1 difference falls from 3.494e-2 to 6.7e-4 (limit 5e-3). Defaults bit-identical: the default step reproduces ADR 0661's 3.494135e-2, the setting is a no-op bit for bit without rotational pairs (Taylor-Green box, the annulus), baseline_hashes and the periodic and sliding suites pass. Four of four mutations caught. No case key (golden); the default not changed (open); the pressure-lag estimate keeps the lagged rotational coupling. Follow-up F-746 (Implicit rotational periodic pairs by default and as a case key).

On ADR 0661's lockstep with the lag removed by ADR 0664's implicit pair in one outer iteration, the sector's largest difference from the annulus falls from 5.89e-3 to 1.10e-4 U_in over 400 steps, within 3.8e-5 of V(6, 0) on every step (limit 3e-4; the first step equal to rounding, 3.8e-15). Defaults bit-identical (the annulus bit for bit with the setting on, ADR 0661's and ADR 0664's numbers reproduced, baseline_hashes and the periodic, sliding and non-orthogonal suites pass). Partial: two of four mutations caught; the pressure part of the correction is below the lockstep's resolution on this flow (at most 2.5e-4 of the coupled-face flux: the wrap faces' k is tangential and the pressure nearly radial), so its effect is not shown; the momentum part carries the result. No case key; the default not changed (open, with F-746). Follow-up F-752 (Pressure part of the non-orthogonal correction on coupled faces).

  - depends on: F-727

Closed form: an impostor honest on m of n pairs is missed with probability C(m,k)/C(n,k); for the 13-pair F-727 sample of 64 pairs, k = 3 (miss 0.0069). Checks on 400 synthetic worlds: an evaluator that reads the registration and is honest exactly on the F-727 sample is caught in 399 (limit 380) with k = 3, one dishonest on 16 pairs outside that sample in 394 (limit 380) with k = 13, while the F-727 sample catches neither, 0 of 800 (negative control); a "verifier" seed derived from the file catches 0 of 400; k = 1 catches 305 (287 to 350); the honest evaluator is never flagged; the problem count equals the drawn dishonest pairs in 800 of 800. Every ADR 0624 and ADR 0662 check keeps its numbers (S1 1, S2 1592 of 1595, NC1 400, NC2 61, S4 118; A1 394, NC6 0, NC7 116, the C2 byte literals). Nine mutations caught. Not covered: a forger who can also append to the ledger (records are not signed), lessons does not read drawn records, no MCP tool (F-702). Follow-up F-776 (Lessons read the verifier-drawn checks). ADR 0695 (F-776, 2026-11-17): lessons_drawn reads the drawn records, so the verifier-drawn check now decides whether a hypothesis is reported.

- [~] **F-763** Rule L loses positive definiteness on the refined neo-Hookean punch block
  - depends on: F-747
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The failing solve of ADR 0678 (rule L, the neo-Hookean material of ADR 0636, the punch block on 16^3, the default options) reproduced first; the lowest eigenvalue of the ADR 0628 sweep and of the free tangent at the last converged state located by element; the same solve with S and W of ADR 0658 and ADR 0660 and with finer increments; the cause identified or bounded against a registered criterion; the default bits unchanged.
  - gap: The cause is bounded, not identified: the failure is at a Newton iterate (later shown to be the predictor's) from a stable converged state under the punch corner, and why one element goes soft is open. The registered hypothesis of an indefinite converged tangent was missed, and one of six mutations is not caught.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier. Follow-up of F-747 (ADR 0678). PARTIAL. ADR 0682, 2026-11-17 (tests only, no library file changed): the failing solve of ADR 0678 (rule L, neo-Hookean, the punch block on 16^3, default options) reproduced to the character, its attempts recorded through an identity step-control hook (last converged load factor 0.9625). The last converged state rebuilt by a replicated path (the driver's predictor, then solve_from; a lifted start was a defective set-up, corrected by amendment): none of the 13 converged states has a negative eigenvalue (supernodal inertia), and the driver's own first factor passes at the last one, so the negative pivot of ADR 0678 belongs to a Newton iterate, not to the equilibrium. The free tangent there: lowest eigenvalue 0.0363 mu h against F-bar's 0.0362 at its own state, F-bar's energy of rule L's mode positive, the mode global and smooth. The ADR 0628 pencil there: lowest 0.063 mu, isolated (next 0.615), in two elements of hourglass form (share 0.88) under the punch corner, where the element with the smallest modes block also sits. S and W fail exactly as the default; 20 and 40 increments fail earlier (0.870, 0.871) by an inverted element under the punch corner. Cause bounded by the registered criterion (a stable converged state, no finer solve passes): not an instability of the body or of rule L at a converged state; a Newton iterate from a stable state at the punch corner, not the edge row; the soft local pencil mode is the candidate, not proven. Missed: the plain element's 8^3 failure, registered as the positive control of a spurious instability, is also at an iterate; the registered hypothesis that the converged tangent is indefinite. Five of six mutations caught. No default bit changed. Not covered: the iterates of the failing attempt, a remedy, a 32^3 mesh. Follow-up F-767 (The failing Newton iterate of rule L at the punch corner). ADR 0688 (F-767, 2026-11-17): the failing iterate of the 16^3 rule L solve is the predictor's; the soft mode is not carried by the predictor (share 4e-27) but turns negative in one element under the punch corner within one small step (F-767).

  - depends on: F-763
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The failing attempt of ADR 0682 (rule L, neo-Hookean, the punch block on 16^3, from the converged state at load factor 0.9625) recorded iterate by iterate: the predictor's share in the isolated pencil mode of ADR 0682 and the lowest eigenvalue of the free tangent and of the ADR 0628 pencil at every iterate, located by element; the ADR 0628 sweep at the state of the punch-corner element; the line search of ADR 0607 and a registered damping of the predictor on the same attempt, and whether the 16^3 block then solves to full load; a positive control on the ADR 0628 patch below its zero; the default bits unchanged.

  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier. Follow-up of F-763 (ADR 0682). PARTIAL. ADR 0688, 2026-11-17: the failing attempt of ADR 0682 (rule L, neo-Hookean, the punch block on 16^3, 0.9625 to 0.965625) recorded iterate by iterate through a contribution that adds nothing (the solve unchanged to the bit) and rebuilt step by step bit for bit; new opt-in NewtonOptions::predictor_damping (the ADR 0607 step-length rule from the lifted iterate, a trial admissible only if its tangent passes the pivot test; default off, defaults bit-identical, baseline_hashes passes) and new public nonlinear::solve_increment (one driver attempt from a committed state, bit for bit the driver's). The attempt fails at the predictor's iterate: the predictor (3.7e-4, its tangent consistent to 1.4e-7, at the energy minimum of its line) is orthogonal to the isolated pencil mode of ADR 0682 (share 4.1e-27), so the candidate of ADR 0682 is refuted; at that iterate the tangent has one negative eigenvalue (-0.076 mu h; the ADR 0628 pencil -0.029 mu, from +0.063 at the converged state) in the single element 3720 under the punch corner, hourglass form (share 0.93), with nothing else moved and no jump of the modes. The ADR 0628 sweep at the centre gradients of the corner elements 3959 and 3720 is stable (m_L 1.057 and 1.060, zero only 40 to 50 per cent further along the ray): not a homogeneous-state property. The line search cannot act on the predictor; the damping falls back to the full step because the lifted iterate inverts the corner element 3959 (a probe); no remedy (line search, damping, both) solves the 16^3 block to full load. Positive control: the plain element on the ADR 0628 patch at 0.93 (below its zero 0.9507) has 21 negative eigenvalues, found by the sparse tools equal to the dense ones to 1.2e-15. Missed: the pencil of one negative control (the plain element at 0.97) not converged in 300 iterations; two of seven mutations not caught. Not covered: the equilibrium at 0.965625 (the driver refuses an indefinite tangent), a change of rule L's coefficient (the maintainer's call), other meshes.
